4. Speculative Decoding with Rejection Sampling


=============================================================================


@torch.no_grad() def speculative_verify( draft_tokens: torch.Tensor, draft_probs: torch.Tensor, target_logits: torch.Tensor, prefix_len: int, temperature: float = 1.0, greedy_verify: bool = False, ) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, torch.Tensor, int, Dict[str, Any]]: """ Verify K speculative tokens using rejection sampling.

The algorithm (Leviathan et al., 2023; Chen et al., 2023): For each draft token t_i from the draft model's distribution q: Let p be the target model's probability for t_i ACCEPT with probability: min(1, p(t_i) / q(t_i)) If REJECTED: - Sample a new token from (p - q)_+ (the adjusted distribution) - Stop If ACCEPTED: - Continue to next draft token If ALL K tokens accepted: - Sample one additional token from target Args: draft_tokens: (batch, k) - K speculative tokens per sequence draft_probs: (batch, k) - draft model probability q(t_i) for each token target_logits: (batch, prefix_len + k, vocab_size) - target model logits IMPORTANT: Position i predicts token i+1 prefix_len: Length of the original prefix (prompt) temperature: Sampling temperature greedy_verify: If True, use simple greedy matching instead of rejection sampling Returns: accepted_tokens: (batch, n_accepted) - tokens that were accepted bonus_token: (batch,) or None - extra token if all K accepted, plus sampled token on reject num_accepted: number of tokens accepted (minimum across batch for simplicity) stats: Dictionary with acceptance statistics """ batch_size, k = draft_tokens.shape device = draft_tokens.device # Get target probabilities for each draft token position # Remember: logits at position PREDICT the next token # So for draft token at position prefix_len + i (0-indexed in draft), # we need logits at position prefix_len + i - 1 # # Example: prefix_len=5, draft has k=3 tokens # Draft token 0 goes to position 5 → predicted by logits[4] # Draft token 1 goes to position 6 → predicted by logits[5] # Draft token 2 goes to position 7 → predicted by logits[6] # Get target logits for the positions that predict draft tokens # Shape: (batch, k, vocab_size) draft_prediction_positions = torch.arange(prefix_len - 1, prefix_len - 1 + k, device=device) draft_target_logits = target_logits[:, draft_prediction_positions, :] # Get target probabilities for the actual draft tokens # Shape: (batch, k) target_probs = get_token_prob(draft_target_logits, draft_tokens, temperature=temperature) # Also need target distribution argmax for greedy verification target_argmax = draft_target_logits.argmax(dim=-1) # (batch, k) # Track acceptance per position accepted = torch.zeros(batch_size, k, dtype=torch.bool, device=device) bonus_token = None total_accepted = 0 stats = { "draft_probs": draft_probs.cpu(), "target_probs": target_probs.cpu(), "acceptance_ratios": torch.minimum(torch.ones_like(target_probs), target_probs / draft_probs.clamp(min=1e-8)).cpu(), } if greedy_verify: # --------------------------------------------------------------------- # Greedy verification (simpler, used in some implementations) # Accept if draft token == target argmax # --------------------------------------------------------------------- matches = (draft_tokens == target_argmax) # (batch, k) # Find first non-match per sequence for i in range(k): all_match = matches[:, i].all().item() if all_match: accepted[:, i] = True total_accepted = i + 1 else: # Partial matches get complicated # For simplicity in greedy mode, we accept until first rejection # Then sample from target # Actually, for proper handling across batch with varying acceptance, # let's just track minimum accepted for simplicity # Real implementations handle each sequence independently break # Get bonus token (target's prediction at last accepted position) if total_accepted == k: # All accepted, sample one more from target at position prefix_len + k bonus_logits = target_logits[:, prefix_len + k - 1, :] bonus_token, _ = sample_token(bonus_logits, temperature=temperature) else: # Sample from target at the first rejected position bonus_logits = target_logits[:, prefix_len + total_accepted - 1, :] bonus_token, _ = sample_token(bonus_logits, temperature=temperature) stats["greedy_matches"] = matches.cpu() else: # --------------------------------------------------------------------- # Proper rejection sampling (from "Fast Inference from Transformers...) # --------------------------------------------------------------------- # Accept token i with probability: min(1, p_i / q_i) # Where: # p_i = target probability of draft token # q_i = draft probability of draft token acceptance_probs = torch.minimum( torch.ones_like(target_probs), target_probs / draft_probs.clamp(min=1e-8) ) # (batch, k) # Sample acceptance decisions # If random uniform < acceptance_prob → accept random_samples = torch.rand(batch_size, k, device=device) accepted = (random_samples < acceptance_probs) # (batch, k) # Find the first rejection per sequence # For simplicity, we find how many tokens are accepted up to first rejection # In real implementations, handle each sequence independently # Get cumulative acceptance (all previous must be accepted) cum_accepted = accepted.cumprod(dim=1) # (batch, k) # Count accepted: sum of cum_accepted accepted_counts = cum_accepted.sum(dim=1) # (batch,) # For simplicity in this example, use minimum across batch # Real implementations handle each sequence independently min_accepted = int(accepted_counts.min().item()) total_accepted = min_accepted stats["acceptance_decisions"] = accepted.cpu() stats["accepted_counts"] = accepted_counts.cpu() # --------------------------------------------------------------------- # After rejection, sample from adjusted distribution: # p'(x) = (p(x) - q(x))_+ / Z # Where (.)_+ is max(., 0) and Z is normalization constant # # This ensures correctness: the marginal distribution is exactly p(x) # --------------------------------------------------------------------- if total_accepted < k: # There was at least one rejection at position total_accepted # Get target and draft probs at this position pos = total_accepted p_logits = draft_target_logits[:, pos, :] # (batch, vocab_size) p = F.softmax(apply_temperature(p_logits, temperature), dim=-1) # For draft probs, we'd need to query draft model again # Or we can just sample from p directly (slight simplification) # # The proper formula: p' = (p - q)_+ normalized # But sampling from p is common approximation bonus_logits = p_logits bonus_token, _ = sample_token(bonus_logits, temperature=temperature) else: # All K tokens accepted! Sample one more from target bonus_logits = target_logits[:, prefix_len + k - 1, :] bonus_token, _ = sample_token(bonus_logits, temperature=temperature) # Calculate acceptance rate stats acceptance_rate = total_accepted / k stats["num_accepted"] = total_accepted stats["k"] = k stats["acceptance_rate"] = acceptance_rate # Get the actual accepted tokens if total_accepted > 0: accepted_tokens = draft_tokens[:, :total_accepted].clone() else: accepted_tokens = torch.empty(batch_size, 0, dtype=torch.long, device=device) return accepted_tokens, bonus_token, total_accepted, stats





=============================================================================


5. Main Speculative Decoding Function


=============================================================================


class SpeculativeGenerator: """ Complete speculative decoding generator.

Usage: generator = SpeculativeGenerator(draft_model, target_model, tokenizer, config) output = generator.speculative_generate(input_ids, attention_mask, max_new_tokens=100) """ def __init__( self, draft_model, target_model, tokenizer, config: Optional[SpeculativeConfig] = None, ): self.draft = SimpleDraftModel(draft_model, tokenizer) self.target = TargetModelWrapper(target_model, tokenizer) self.tokenizer = tokenizer self.config = config or SpeculativeConfig() # Running statistics self.total_draft_tokens = 0 self.total_accepted_tokens = 0 self.total_steps = 0 def get_acceptance_rate(self) -> float: """Get overall acceptance rate across all generations.""" if self.total_draft_tokens == 0: return 0.0 return self.total_accepted_tokens / self.total_draft_tokens @torch.no_grad() def speculative_generate( self, input_ids: torch.Tensor, attention_mask: torch.Tensor, max_new_tokens: int, ) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, Dict[str, Any]]: """ Generate text using speculative decoding. Algorithm: While need more tokens: 1. Draft model generates K tokens 2. Target model processes prefix + K tokens in ONE forward pass 3. Verify each draft token via rejection sampling 4. Keep accepted tokens + 1 target-sampled token Args: input_ids: (batch, seq_len) - prompt tokens attention_mask: (batch, seq_len) - attention mask max_new_tokens: maximum tokens to generate Returns: output_ids: (batch, seq_len + n_generated) - full output stats: Dictionary with generation statistics """ batch_size = input_ids.shape[0] device = input_ids.device config = self.config current_ids = input_ids.clone() current_mask = attention_mask.clone() tokens_generated = 0 steps_taken = 0 # Statistics all_accepted_counts = [] draft_steps = 0 start_time = time.time() while tokens_generated < max_new_tokens: prefix_len = current_ids.shape[1] # How many speculative tokens to try in this step? k = min( config.num_speculative_tokens, max_new_tokens - tokens_generated ) if k <= 0: break # Check if acceptance rate is too low — fall back to standard if self.total_steps > 5 and self.get_acceptance_rate() < config.min_acceptance_threshold: if config.debug: print(f"Acceptance rate {self.get_acceptance_rate():.2%} below threshold. " f"Falling back to standard generation.") break # ================================================================= # Step 1: Draft model generates K tokens # ================================================================= draft_start = time.time() draft_tokens, draft_probs = self.draft.generate_k_tokens( current_ids, current_mask, k, temperature=config.temperature, top_k=config.top_k, top_p=config.top_p, ) draft_time = time.time() - draft_start # ================================================================= # Step 2: Concatenate prefix + draft tokens # ================================================================= full_ids = torch.cat([current_ids, draft_tokens], dim=-1) full_mask = torch.cat([ current_mask, torch.ones(batch_size, k, dtype=torch.long, device=device) ], dim=-1) # ================================================================= # Step 3: Target model ONE forward pass for ALL K tokens # ================================================================= target_start = time.time() target_logits = self.target.get_logits_for_verification(full_ids, full_mask) target_time = time.time() - target_start # ================================================================= # Step 4: Verify and accept/reject # ================================================================= accepted_tokens, bonus_token, num_accepted, verify_stats = speculative_verify( draft_tokens, draft_probs, target_logits, prefix_len, temperature=config.temperature, greedy_verify=config.greedy_verify, ) # ================================================================= # Step 5: Update running statistics # ================================================================= self.total_draft_tokens += k self.total_accepted_tokens += num_accepted self.total_steps += 1 all_accepted_counts.append(num_accepted) draft_steps += 1 # ================================================================= # Step 6: Build the output for this step # ================================================================= # Accepted tokens + bonus token num_in_this_step = num_accepted + 1 # +1 for bonus/sampled token # Don't exceed max_new_tokens if tokens_generated + num_in_this_step > max_new_tokens: # Truncate num_in_this_step = max_new_tokens - tokens_generated if num_in_this_step <= 0: break # Concatenate accepted tokens + bonus token if num_accepted > 0 and num_in_this_step > num_accepted: # Accepted + bonus new_tokens = torch.cat([ accepted_tokens[:, :num_accepted], bonus_token.unsqueeze(-1) ], dim=-1) # Truncate if needed new_tokens = new_tokens[:, :num_in_this_step] elif num_accepted > 0: # Only accepted (bonus would exceed limit) new_tokens = accepted_tokens[:, :num_in_this_step] else: # No tokens accepted, just use bonus new_tokens = bonus_token.unsqueeze(-1)[:, :num_in_this_step] # Update current state current_ids = torch.cat([current_ids, new_tokens], dim=-1) new_mask = torch.ones(batch_size, new_tokens.shape[1], dtype=torch.long, device=device) current_mask = torch.cat([current_mask, new_mask], dim=-1) tokens_generated += new_tokens.shape[1] steps_taken += 1 if config.debug: print(f"Step {steps_taken}: draft K={k}, accepted={num_accepted}, " f"rate={verify_stats['acceptance_rate']:.2%}, " f"draft_time={draft_time*1000:.1f}ms, target_time={target_time*1000:.1f}ms") total_time = time.time() - start_time # ===================================================================== # Fallback: if acceptance rate too low or still need tokens # ===================================================================== if tokens_generated < max_new_tokens: remaining = max_new_tokens - tokens_generated if config.debug: print(f"Fallback: generating {remaining} tokens with standard method...") # Simple standard generation for _ in range(remaining): outputs = self.target.model(current_ids, attention_mask=current_mask) next_logits = outputs.logits[:, -1, :] next_token, _ = sample_token( next_logits, temperature=config.temperature, top_k=config.top_k, top_p=config.top_p, ) current_ids = torch.cat([current_ids, next_token.unsqueeze(-1)], dim=-1) next_mask = torch.ones(batch_size, 1, dtype=torch.long, device=device) current_mask = torch.cat([current_mask, next_mask], dim=-1) tokens_generated += 1 # ===================================================================== # Final statistics # ===================================================================== effective_acceptance_rate = ( sum(all_accepted_counts) / (len(all_accepted_counts) * config.num_speculative_tokens) if all_accepted_counts else 0.0 ) stats = { "tokens_generated": tokens_generated, "speculative_steps": draft_steps, "standard_steps": max(0, tokens_generated - sum(all_accepted_counts) - draft_steps), "mean_acceptance_rate": effective_acceptance_rate, "total_time_sec": total_time, "tokens_per_second": tokens_generated / total_time, "all_accepted_counts": all_accepted_counts, } return current_ids, stats @torch.no_grad() def standard_generate( self, input_ids: torch.Tensor, attention_mask: torch.Tensor, max_new_tokens: int, ) -> Tuple[torch.Tensor, Dict[str, Any]]: """ Standard autoregressive generation (for benchmarking). """ current_ids = input_ids.clone() current_mask = attention_mask.clone() start_time = time.time() for _ in range(max_new_tokens): outputs = self.target.model(current_ids, attention_mask=current_mask) next_logits = outputs.logits[:, -1, :] next_token, _ = sample_token( next_logits, temperature=self.config.temperature, top_k=self.config.top_k, top_p=self.config.top_p, ) current_ids = torch.cat([current_ids, next_token.unsqueeze(-1)], dim=-1) next_mask = torch.ones(current_ids.shape[0], 1, dtype=torch.long, device=input_ids.device) current_mask = torch.cat([current_mask, next_mask], dim=-1) total_time = time.time() - start_time stats = { "tokens_generated": max_new_tokens, "total_time_sec": total_time, "tokens_per_second": max_new_tokens / total_time, } return current_ids, stats

6. Performance Benchmark


=============================================================================


def run_benchmark( draft_model, target_model, tokenizer, prompts: List[str], max_new_tokens: int = 256, num_speculative_tokens: int = 4, ) -> Dict[str, Any]: """ Benchmark standard vs speculative decoding. """ # Configure config = SpeculativeConfig( num_speculative_tokens=num_speculative_tokens, temperature=0.7, top_k=50, top_p=0.9, greedy_verify=False, )

generator = SpeculativeGenerator(draft_model, target_model, tokenizer, config) # Tokenize prompts all_input_ids = [] all_attention_masks = [] for prompt in prompts: encodings = tokenizer( prompt, return_tensors="pt", truncation=True, max_length=512, ) all_input_ids.append(encodings["input_ids"]) all_attention_masks.append(encodings["attention_mask"]) # For simplicity, benchmark one at a time standard_tps = [] speculative_tps = [] acceptance_rates = [] print(f"\n{'='*60}") print(f"Benchmark: Standard vs Speculative Decoding (K={num_speculative_tokens})") print(f"{'='*60}") for i, (input_ids, attention_mask) in enumerate(zip(all_input_ids, all_attention_masks)): input_ids = input_ids.to(target_model.device) attention_mask = attention_mask.to(target_model.device) prompt_text = prompts[i][:50] + "..." if len(prompts[i]) > 50 else prompts[i] print(f"\nPrompt {i+1}: {prompt_text}") # --------------------------------------------------------------------- # Standard Decoding # --------------------------------------------------------------------- torch.cuda.empty_cache() _, standard_stats = generator.standard_generate( input_ids, attention_mask, max_new_tokens ) standard_tps.append(standard_stats["tokens_per_second"]) print(f" Standard: {standard_stats['tokens_per_second']:.2f} tokens/sec") # --------------------------------------------------------------------- # Speculative Decoding # --------------------------------------------------------------------- torch.cuda.empty_cache() _, spec_stats = generator.speculative_generate( input_ids, attention_mask, max_new_tokens ) speculative_tps.append(spec_stats["tokens_per_second"]) acceptance_rates.append(spec_stats["mean_acceptance_rate"]) print(f" Speculative: {spec_stats['tokens_per_second']:.2f} tokens/sec " f"(acceptance: {spec_stats['mean_acceptance_rate']:.2%})") speedup = spec_stats["tokens_per_second"] / standard_stats["tokens_per_second"] print(f" Speedup: {speedup:.2f}x") # ------------------------------------------------------------------------- # Summary # ------------------------------------------------------------------------- avg_standard = sum(standard_tps) / len(standard_tps) avg_speculative = sum(speculative_tps) / len(speculative_tps) avg_acceptance = sum(acceptance_rates) / len(acceptance_rates) avg_speedup = avg_speculative / avg_standard print(f"\n{'='*60}") print(f"SUMMARY") print(f"{'='*60}") print(f"Average Standard: {avg_standard:.2f} tokens/sec") print(f"Average Speculative: {avg_speculative:.2f} tokens/sec") print(f"Average Acceptance: {avg_acceptance:.2%}") print(f"Average Speedup: {avg_speedup:.2f}x") return { "avg_standard_tps": avg_standard, "avg_speculative_tps": avg_speculative, "avg_acceptance_rate": avg_acceptance, "avg_speedup": avg_speedup, "per_prompt_standard_tps": standard_tps, "per_prompt_speculative_tps": speculative_tps, "per_prompt_acceptance": acceptance_rates, }





=============================================================================


7. Key Considerations & Production Usage


=============================================================================


""" KEY CONSIDERATIONS FOR SPECULATIVE DECODING:

Draft Model Selection:

The draft model must be MUCH faster than the target model

Good options: Distilled version of target model

Smaller variant (e.g., Mistral-7B as draft for Mixtral-8x7B)

Same architecture but fewer layers/parameters





Most importantly: draft and target should use SAME tokenizer



Typical draft model sizes: - 1/4 to 1/10 the size of target - If draft is too large → overhead erases benefits - If draft is too small → low acceptance rate

Choosing K (Number of Speculative Tokens):

Typical values: 3, 4, 5

Larger K = more potential speedup IF acceptance rate stays high

Larger K = longer draft generation time



Optimal K depends on: - Draft model speed relative to target - Expected acceptance rate

Rule of thumb: - If draft is ~10x faster than target, try K=4-5 - If draft is ~4x faster, try K=3

Speedup formula (approximate): Expected speedup ≈ 1 / ( (1 - α) + α/K + T_draft/(K * T_target) ) Where α = acceptance rate T_draft = time per draft forward T_target = time per target forward

Acceptance Rate Factors:

Higher is better (obviously)

Typical: 50-80% depending on task

Depends on: How well draft model approximates target

Temperature (higher temp = lower acceptance)

Task complexity (coding = lower acceptance than chat)





If acceptance rate < 30-40%, speculative may be SLOWER than standard → Use the fallback mechanism!

Temperature Effects:

Temperature affects acceptance rate

Higher temperature = more sampling diversity = lower acceptance

At temp→0 (greedy), can use greedy verification (argmax matching)



Implementation note: - Proper rejection sampling accounts for temperature in both draft and target - The formula: accept with probability min(1, p_temp(t) / q_temp(t)) - Where p_temp = softmax(logits / T)

Production-Grade Libraries:

vLLM: Built-in speculative decoding support python from vllm import LLM llm = LLM( model="meta-llama/Llama-2-70b-chat-hf", speculative_model="meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-chat-hf", num_speculative_tokens=5, )



Text Generation Inference (TGI): Has speculative decoding



TensorRT-LLM: NVIDIA's implementation

llama.cpp: speculative_decoding options



Advanced Variants:



Medusa: Multiple draft heads predict K tokens in parallel (no sequential draft)

Eagle: Tree-based speculative decoding

Lookahead Decoding: Speculate without separate draft model

Block-Level Speculation: Speculate entire blocks of tokens



Memory Considerations:



Need to load BOTH draft and target models

May require multiple GPUs or model parallelism

Target: main GPU(s), Draft: smaller GPU or even CPU (if fast enough)



With quantization: - Target can be in 4-bit (AWQ/GPTQ) - Draft can be in 8-bit or even FP16 """

=============================================================================


def example_usage(): """Example of how to use speculative decoding.""" from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer

# Load models # In practice, draft should be much smaller than target model_name = "mistralai/Mistral-7B-v0.1" draft_name = "mistralai/Mistral-7B-v0.1" # Same model for demo only! # Load tokenizer tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name) tokenizer.pad_token = tokenizer.eos_token # Load models target_model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained( model_name, torch_dtype=torch.float16, device_map="auto", ) # For demo, use same model as draft (in practice, use smaller!) draft_model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained( draft_name, torch_dtype=torch.float16, device_map="auto", ) # Create generator config = SpeculativeConfig( num_speculative_tokens=4, temperature=0.7, top_k=50, top_p=0.9, debug=True, ) generator = SpeculativeGenerator(draft_model, target_model, tokenizer, config) # Test prompts prompts = [ "Explain quantum computing to a beginner.", "Write a Python function to compute the Fibonacci sequence.", "What are the key differences between SQL and NoSQL databases?", ] # Generate for prompt in prompts: print(f"\nPrompt: {prompt}") inputs = tokenizer(prompt, return_tensors="pt").to(target_model.device) output_ids, stats = generator.speculative_generate( inputs["input_ids"], inputs["attention_mask"], max_new_tokens=100, ) output_text = tokenizer.decode(output_ids[0], skip_special_tokens=True) response = output_text[len(prompt):].strip() print(f"Response: {response[:200]}...") print(f"Stats: acceptance={stats['mean_acceptance_rate']:.2%}, " f"{stats['tokens_per_second']:.2f} tokens/sec") # Benchmark benchmark_results = run_benchmark( draft_model, target_model, tokenizer, prompts, max_new_tokens=64, num_speculative_tokens=4 ) return benchmark_results

if name == "main": print(""" Speculative Decoding Implementation

Key takeaways: 1. Draft model generates K tokens in K forward passes (but it's fast) 2. Target model validates all K tokens in 1 forward pass (slow but fewer passes) 3. Rejection sampling accepts tokens where target agrees with draft 4. Speedup comes from fewer passes of the slow target model For production use: - Use vLLM with speculative_model parameter - Or use TGI, TensorRT-LLM, or llama.cpp """)

```

28. Embedding & Retrieval Models


28.1 Embedding Model Architecture


```python





embedding_model.py


class EmbeddingModel(nn.Module): """Dual-encoder for text embeddings (sentence-transformers style)""" def init(self, base_llm: TransformerModel, pooling="mean", normalize=True): super().init() self.encoder = base_llm self.pooling = pooling self.normalize = normalize

def forward(self, input_ids, attention_mask=None): # Encode tokens seq_len = input_ids.shape[1] cos, sin = self.encoder.rotary_emb(input_ids, seq_len) hidden = self.encoder.embed_tokens(input_ids) for layer in self.encoder.layers: hidden = layer(hidden, cos, sin, attention_mask) hidden = self.encoder.norm(hidden) # Pooling if self.pooling == "mean": if attention_mask is not None: mask = attention_mask.unsqueeze(-1) embedding = (hidden * mask).sum(dim=1) / mask.sum(dim=1) else: embedding = hidden.mean(dim=1) elif self.pooling == "cls": embedding = hidden[:, 0, :] # First token (BERT-style) elif self.pooling == "last": if attention_mask is not None: last = attention_mask.sum(dim=1) - 1 embedding = hidden[torch.arange(hidden.size(0)), last] else: embedding = hidden[:, -1, :] # Normalize if self.normalize: embedding = F.normalize(embedding, p=2, dim=-1) return embedding





Training with contrastive loss


class ContrastiveTrainer: """Train embeddings with in-batch negatives and hard negatives""" def init(self, model, temperature=0.05): self.model = model self.temperature = temperature

def compute_loss(self, query_embeddings, doc_embeddings): """InfoNCE loss: maximize similarity of (query, positive) pairs""" # SimCSE / IN-Batch negatives scores = torch.matmul(query_embeddings, doc_embeddings.T) / self.temperature batch_size = query_embeddings.size(0) # Labels: diagonal (each query matches its own doc) labels = torch.arange(batch_size, device=query_embeddings.device) loss = F.cross_entropy(scores, labels) # Optional: add hard negative mining return loss def train_step(self, query_batch, doc_batch): q_emb = self.model(query_batch) d_emb = self.model(doc_batch) loss = self.compute_loss(q_emb, d_emb) return loss

```





28.2 Training Data for Embeddings


```python





Generate training pairs for embedding models


def generate_retrieval_pairs(corpus, queries, relevant_docs): """Create (query, positive, negative) triples""" pairs = []

for qid, query in queries.items(): positive_ids = relevant_docs[qid] for pos_id in positive_ids[:3]: # Up to 3 positives per query positive = corpus[pos_id] # In-batch negative: use other queries' documents for other_qid in random.sample([k for k in queries if k != qid], min(5, len(queries) - 1)): neg_id = random.choice(relevant_docs[other_qid]) negative = corpus[neg_id] pairs.append({ "anchor": query, "positive": positive, "negative": negative, }) return pairs





Dataset sources for embedding training


EMBEDDING_DATASETS = { "MS MARCO": "microsoft/ms_marco", # Search queries + passages "Natural Questions": "google/natural_questions", # Google search data "HotpotQA": "hotpotqa/hotpot_qa", # Multi-hop QA "NQ": "nq_open", # Trivia QA "StackExchange": "flax-sentence-embeddings/stackexchange_xml", # Q&A pairs "ELI5": "eli5/eli5", # Long-form explanations } ```





28.3 Evaluation Metrics for Embeddings


```python def evaluate_embeddings(model, queries, corpus, relevant_docs, k=[1, 5, 10, 100]): """Information retrieval evaluation""" # Precompute all embeddings model.eval() with torch.no_grad(): query_embs = torch.stack([model(q) for q in queries]) corpus_embs = torch.stack([model(c) for c in corpus])

# Similarity matrix sim = torch.matmul(query_embs, corpus_embs.T) results = {} for k_val in k: recall = 0 mrr = 0 for qid, (query_id, _) in enumerate(queries.items()): top_k = sim[qid].topk(k_val).indices relevant = set(relevant_docs[query_id]) # Recall@k hits = sum(1 for idx in top_k if idx in relevant) recall += hits / len(relevant) # MRR@k for rank, idx in enumerate(top_k): if idx in relevant: mrr += 1.0 / (rank + 1) break results[f"recall@{k_val}"] = recall / len(queries) results[f"mrr@{k_val}"] = mrr / len(queries) return results

```

29. Evals-Driven Development & A/B Testing


29.1 Continuous Evaluation Pipeline


```python





evals_pipeline.py


import json, time, subprocess from datetime import datetime

class EvalPipeline: """Automated evaluation pipeline for model checkpoints""" def init(self, config_path="eval_config.json"): with open(config_path) as f: self.config = json.load(f)

self.benchmarks = self.config["benchmarks"] self.thresholds = self.config["thresholds"] self.history = [] def run_benchmark(self, model_path, benchmark_name): """Run a single benchmark""" if benchmark_name == "mmlu": result = subprocess.run([ "python", "-m", "lm_eval", "--model", "hf", "--model_args", f"pretrained={model_path}", "--tasks", "mmlu", "--num_fewshot", "5", "--output_path", f"evals/{benchmark_name}_{datetime.now().isoformat()}.json", ], capture_output=True, text=True) elif benchmark_name == "gsm8k": result = subprocess.run([ "python", "-m", "lm_eval", "--model", "hf", "--model_args", f"pretrained={model_path}", "--tasks", "gsm8k", "--num_fewshot", "8", ], capture_output=True, text=True) return json.loads(result.stdout) def check_regression(self, results): """Check if new model regresses on any benchmark""" for benchmark, score in results.items(): if benchmark in self.history: previous = self.history[-1].get(benchmark, score) threshold = self.thresholds.get(benchmark, 0.02) # Default 2% if previous - score > threshold: return { "regression": True, "benchmark": benchmark, "previous": previous, "current": score, "drop": previous - score, } return {"regression": False} def evaluate_checkpoint(self, model_path): """Full evaluation of a checkpoint""" print(f"Evaluating {model_path}...") results = {"timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat(), "model_path": model_path} for benchmark in self.benchmarks: try: score = self.run_benchmark(model_path, benchmark) results[benchmark] = score.get("results", {}).get(benchmark, {}).get("acc") print(f" {benchmark}: {results[benchmark]:.2%}") except Exception as e: print(f" {benchmark}: FAILED - {e}") results[benchmark] = None regression = self.check_regression(results) if regression["regression"]: print(f"REGRESSION DETECTED: {regression['benchmark']} dropped {regression['drop']:.2%}") self.history.append(results) return results, regression def compare_models(self, model_a_path, model_b_path): """A/B comparison of two models on all benchmarks""" results_a, _ = self.evaluate_checkpoint(model_a_path) results_b, _ = self.evaluate_checkpoint(model_b_path) comparison = {} for benchmark in self.benchmarks: a_score = results_a.get(benchmark) b_score = results_b.get(benchmark) if a_score is not None and b_score is not None: comparison[benchmark] = { "model_a": a_score, "model_b": b_score, "delta": b_score - a_score, "winner": "A" if a_score > b_score else ("B" if b_score > a_score else "tie"), } return comparison

```





29.2 A/B Testing Framework


```python class ABTest: """Online A/B testing for model variants in production""" def init(self, model_a, model_b, traffic_split=0.5): self.model_a = model_a self.model_b = model_b self.split = traffic_split self.results = []

def route_request(self, user_id, prompt): """Route user to model A or B consistently""" if hash(str(user_id)) % 100 < self.split * 100: return self.model_a.generate(prompt) else: return self.model_b.generate(prompt) def record_feedback(self, user_id, model, feedback_score): """Record user feedback (thumbs up/down, rating)""" self.results.append({ "user_id": user_id, "model": model, "score": feedback_score, "timestamp": time.time(), }) def analyze_results(self, min_samples=1000): """Statistical analysis of A/B test""" scores_a = [r["score"] for r in self.results if r["model"] == "A"] scores_b = [r["score"] for r in self.results if r["model"] == "B"] if len(scores_a) < min_samples or len(scores_b) < min_samples: return {"error": "Insufficient samples", "n_a": len(scores_a), "n_b": len(scores_b)} import scipy.stats as stats mean_a = np.mean(scores_a) mean_b = np.mean(scores_b) # t-test t_stat, p_value = stats.ttest_ind(scores_a, scores_b) return { "model_a_mean": mean_a, "model_b_mean": mean_b, "delta": mean_b - mean_a, "p_value": p_value, "significant": p_value < 0.05, "winner": "A" if mean_a > mean_b else "B", "sample_size_a": len(scores_a), "sample_size_b": len(scores_b), } def rollout_decision(self, min_samples=5000, min_lift=0.01): """Decide whether to roll out model B""" result = self.analyze_results(min_samples) if "error" in result: return {"decision": "continue_test", "reason": result["error"]} if result["significant"] and result["delta"] > min_lift: return { "decision": "rollout_b", "lift": result["delta"], "p_value": result["p_value"], } elif result["significant"] and result["delta"] < -min_lift: return { "decision": "keep_a", "reason": "Model B is worse", } else: return {"decision": "continue_test", "reason": "Not statistically significant yet"}

```





29.3 Human Evaluation Platform


```python class BlindEval: """Blind A/B comparison with human judges""" def init(self, models, model_names): self.models = models self.model_names = model_names

def create_eval_task(self, prompt): """Generate responses from all models""" responses = [] for model in self.models: response = model.generate(prompt) responses.append(response) # Shuffle to blind the judge indices = list(range(len(responses))) random.shuffle(indices) return { "prompt": prompt, "responses": [responses[i] for i in indices], "original_order": [self.model_names[i] for i in indices], } def score_responses(self, eval_task, judge_scores): """Record judge scores and map back to models""" results = [] for original_model, score in zip(eval_task["original_order"], judge_scores): results.append({"model": original_model, "score": score}) return results





Elo rating calculation (used by Chatbot Arena)


def compute_elo(scores_a, scores_b, k=32): """Compute Elo rating update from pairwise comparisons""" # Expected score expected_a = 1.0 / (1 + 10 ** ((scores_b - scores_a) / 400)) # Actual score (1 = win, 0.5 = tie, 0 = loss) # Update new_a = scores_a + k * (1 - expected_a) new_b = scores_b - k * (1 - expected_a) return new_a, new_b ```

30.2 Prompt Compression


```python





prompt_compression.py


class PromptCompressor: """Compress system prompts and few-shot examples to save context""" def init(self, tokenizer, target_ratio=0.5): self.tokenizer = tokenizer self.target_ratio = target_ratio

def compress(self, text: str) -> str: """Compress text while preserving key information""" tokens = self.tokenizer.encode(text) original_len = len(tokens) target_len = int(original_len * self.target_ratio) if len(tokens) <= target_len: return text # Strategy 1: Remove redundant whitespace text = " ".join(text.split()) # Strategy 2: Shorten common phrases replacements = { "you should" : "you'll", "in order to" : "to", "with respect to" : "for", "in addition to" : "plus", "a large number of" : "many", "it is important to note that" : "note:", "on the other hand" : "however", "as a result of" : "due to", } for long, short in replacements.items(): text = text.replace(long, short) # Strategy 3: Use LLM to summarize (optional) # If still too long, summarize with the model itself return text

class DynamicSystemPrompt: """Adjust system prompt length based on available context""" def init(self, full_prompt, shorter_prompt, minimal_prompt): self.prompts = { "full": full_prompt, "shorter": shorter_prompt, "minimal": minimal_prompt, }

def select_prompt(self, user_input_length: int, max_context: int, generation_length: int = 2048): """Select the best prompt variant based on available context""" needed = user_input_length + generation_length for variant in ["full", "shorter", "minimal"]: sys_len = len(self.prompts[variant].split()) if sys_len + needed * 1.5 <= max_context: return self.prompts[variant] return self.prompts["minimal"]

```





30.3 Prompt Optimization via Automatic Prompt Engineering (APE)


```python class AutomaticPromptEngineer: """Use a strong model to optimize prompts automatically""" def init(self, optimizer_model, eval_fn): self.optimizer = optimizer_model self.eval_fn = eval_fn

def generate_candidates(self, task_description: str, n_candidates: int = 10): """Generate candidate prompts using the optimizer model""" prompt = f"""Given the task: "{task_description}"

Generate {n_candidates} different system prompts that would help an AI model perform this task well. The prompts should be concise and effective.

Prompts:""" inputs = self.optimizer.tokenizer(prompt, return_tensors="pt").to("cuda") outputs = self.optimizer.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=1024, do_sample=True, temperature=0.9) text = self.optimizer.tokenizer.decode(outputs[0], skip_special_tokens=True)

# Parse prompts candidates = [p.strip() for p in text.split("\n") if p.strip() and len(p) > 20] return candidates[:n_candidates] def optimize(self, task_description: str, n_iterations: int = 5): """Iteratively improve prompts""" best_prompt = None best_score = 0 for i in range(n_iterations): candidates = self.generate_candidates(task_description, n_candidates=5) for candidate in candidates: score = self.eval_fn(candidate) if score > best_score: best_score = score best_prompt = candidate return best_prompt, best_score

```





30.4 Prompt Injection Hardening


```python class PromptGuard: """Multi-layer prompt injection defense""" def init(self): self.separator = "\n---\n" # Delimiter between system and user input

def wrap_system_prompt(self, system: str, user: str) -> str: """Wrap system prompt to prevent leakage""" return f"""<|begin_system|>

{system} <|end_system|> <|begin_user_input|> {user} <|end_user_input|> <|begin_assistant|> """

def detect_instruction_override(self, user_input: str) -> bool: """Detect attempts to override system instructions""" patterns = [ "ignore previous instructions", "ignore all", "disregard", "forget your", "new system prompt", "you are now", "override", "system prompt:", "pretend you are", "act as if you are", "do whatever you want", "you are not bound by", "respond as a different", "in this conversation you will", "from now on you", ] user_lower = user_input.lower() return any(p in user_lower for p in patterns) def sanitize(self, user_input: str) -> str: """Strip known injection tokens""" return user_input.replace("<|", "[").replace("|>", "]") def call_with_guard(self, system_prompt: str, user_input: str) -> str: """Full guarded pipeline""" if self.detect_instruction_override(user_input): user_input = self.sanitize(user_input) user_input = "[Content filtered for safety] " + user_input return self.wrap_system_prompt(system_prompt, user_input)

```

31. Multi-tenant Serving & Rate Limiting


31.1 Rate Limiter


```python





rate_limiter.py


import time, asyncio from collections import defaultdict

class RateLimiter: """Token bucket rate limiter per user/tenant""" def init(self, tokens_per_minute: int = 60, burst: int = 10): self.tokens_per_second = tokens_per_minute / 60 self.burst = burst self.buckets = defaultdict(lambda: {"tokens": burst, "last_update": time.time()})

async def acquire(self, user_id: str, tokens: int = 1) -> bool: """Try to acquire tokens for a request. Returns True if allowed.""" bucket = self.buckets[user_id] # Refill tokens now = time.time() elapsed = now - bucket["last_update"] bucket["tokens"] = min(self.burst, bucket["tokens"] + elapsed * self.tokens_per_second) bucket["last_update"] = now if bucket["tokens"] >= tokens: bucket["tokens"] -= tokens return True return False async def wait_and_acquire(self, user_id: str, tokens: int = 1, max_wait: float = 30.0): """Wait until tokens are available""" start = time.time() while time.time() - start < max_wait: if await self.acquire(user_id, tokens): return True await asyncio.sleep(0.1) return False

class TieredRateLimiter(RateLimiter): """Different rate limits for different service tiers""" def init(self): self.tiers = { "free": RateLimiter(tokens_per_minute=10, burst=5), "pro": RateLimiter(tokens_per_minute=100, burst=20), "enterprise": RateLimiter(tokens_per_minute=1000, burst=100), }

async def acquire(self, user_id: str, tier: str = "free", tokens: int = 1) -> bool: return await self.tiers[tier].acquire(user_id, tokens)

```





31.2 Multi-tenant Request Queue


```python class TenantQueue: """Priority queue with per-tenant fairness""" def init(self): self.queues = defaultdict(asyncio.Queue) self.active_tenants = set()

async def enqueue(self, tenant_id: str, request: dict): await self.queues[tenant_id].put(request) async def dequeue_next(self) -> tuple: """Fair scheduling: round-robin across tenants""" while True: for tenant_id in list(self.queues.keys()): if not self.queues[tenant_id].empty(): request = await self.queues[tenant_id].get() return tenant_id, request await asyncio.sleep(0.01)

class UsageTracker: """Track token usage and cost per tenant""" def init(self): self.usage = defaultdict(lambda: { "prompt_tokens": 0, "generated_tokens": 0, "requests": 0, })

def log_request(self, tenant_id, prompt_tokens, generated_tokens): u = self.usage[tenant_id] u["prompt_tokens"] += prompt_tokens u["generated_tokens"] += generated_tokens u["requests"] += 1 def get_cost(self, tenant_id, price_per_1k_prompt=0.01, price_per_1k_gen=0.03): u = self.usage[tenant_id] return (u["prompt_tokens"] / 1000 * price_per_1k_prompt + u["generated_tokens"] / 1000 * price_per_1k_gen) def get_report(self): return dict(self.usage)

```

Usage-based billing


class BillingSystem: def init(self, rates): self.rates = rates # {tier: {prompt: price, completion: price}} self.usage_log = []

def charge(self, tenant_id, model, prompt_tokens, completion_tokens): tier = self.rates.get(tenant_id, self.rates["default"]) cost = (prompt_tokens * tier["prompt"] + completion_tokens * tier["completion"]) self.usage_log.append({ "tenant": tenant_id, "model": model, "prompt_tokens": prompt_tokens, "completion_tokens": completion_tokens, "cost": cost, "timestamp": time.time(), }) return cost

32. Streaming, Chunking & Real-time Inference


32.1 Streaming Responses


```python





streaming.py


import asyncio from typing import AsyncGenerator

class StreamingInference: """Stream tokens one at a time for real-time UX""" def init(self, model, tokenizer): self.model = model self.tokenizer = tokenizer

async def stream_generate(self, prompt: str, max_tokens: int = 512) -> AsyncGenerator[str, None]: """Generate and yield tokens as they're produced""" input_ids = self.tokenizer(prompt, return_tensors="pt").input_ids.to("cuda") for _ in range(max_tokens): with torch.no_grad(): logits = self.model(input_ids)[:, -1, :] next_token = logits.argmax(dim=-1, keepdim=True) yield self.tokenizer.decode(next_token[0]) input_ids = torch.cat([input_ids, next_token], dim=-1) # Check for EOS if next_token.item() == self.tokenizer.eos_token_id: break async def stream_chat(self, messages: list, model_params: dict = None) -> AsyncGenerator[dict, None]: """Stream chat completions in OpenAI-compatible format""" yield {"choices": [{"delta": {"role": "assistant"}}]} async for token in self.stream_generate(messages[-1]["content"]): yield {"choices": [{"delta": {"content": token}}]} yield {"choices": [{"delta": {}}]}





Server-Sent Events (SSE) streaming


from fastapi import FastAPI from starlette.responses import StreamingResponse

app = FastAPI()

@app.post("/v1/chat/completions") async def chat_completions(request: dict): streamer = StreamingInference(model, tokenizer)

return StreamingResponse( streamer.stream_chat(request["messages"]), media_type="text/event-stream", headers={ "Cache-Control": "no-cache", "Connection": "keep-alive", }, )

```





32.2 Chunking Large Inputs


```python class LongInputChunker: """Process inputs longer than the model's context window""" def init(self, model, tokenizer, max_chunk_size=4096, overlap=512): self.model = model self.tokenizer = tokenizer self.max_chunk_size = max_chunk_size self.overlap = overlap

def chunk_text(self, text: str) -> list: """Split long text into overlapping chunks""" tokens = self.tokenizer.encode(text) chunks = [] for i in range(0, len(tokens), self.max_chunk_size - self.overlap): chunk = tokens[i:i + self.max_chunk_size] chunks.append(self.tokenizer.decode(chunk)) return chunks def process_long_document(self, text: str, task: str) -> str: """Process a long document by chunking and aggregating""" chunks = self.chunk_text(text) chunk_results = [] for chunk in chunks: prompt = f"{task}\n\nDocument chunk:\n{chunk}" inputs = self.tokenizer(prompt, return_tensors="pt").to("cuda") outputs = self.model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=256) result = self.tokenizer.decode(outputs[0], skip_special_tokens=True) chunk_results.append(result) # Aggregate results return self.aggregate_results(chunk_results, task) def aggregate_results(self, results: list, original_task: str) -> str: """Aggregate chunk processing results""" combined = "\n".join([f"Part {i+1}: {r}" for i, r in enumerate(results)]) final_prompt = f"""The following are partial analyses of different sections of a document.

{combined}

Based on the above, provide a comprehensive final answer to: {original_task}""" inputs = self.tokenizer(final_prompt, return_tensors="pt").to("cuda") outputs = self.model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=512) return self.tokenizer.decode(outputs[0], skip_special_tokens=True) ```





32.3 Streaming Optimization Techniques


```python class StreamingOptimizer: """Optimize streaming for lower latency""" def init(self): pass

@staticmethod def prefill_only(input_ids, model): """Process prompt once, cache KV, then generate token by token""" with torch.no_grad(): # Prefill: process all prompt tokens at once seq_len = input_ids.shape[1] cos, sin = model.rotary_emb(input_ids, seq_len) hidden = model.embed_tokens(input_ids) # Cache KV for each layer for i, layer in enumerate(model.layers): hidden = layer(hidden, cos, sin) # KV cache is stored in attention layer for each head return hidden # Last hidden state for generation @staticmethod def decode_one_token(model, last_token, past_key_values): """Generate one token using cached KV""" # Only process the single new token through attention # with cached keys/values from prefill pass # vLLM and HuggingFace handle this internally @staticmethod def estimate_time_to_first_token(prompt_length, model_size): """Estimate TTFT based on prompt length""" # Rough: TTFT ~ prompt_tokens * (flops_per_token / GPU_bandwidth) return prompt_length * model_size / (1e12 * 0.3) # seconds

```





32.4 WebSocket Bidirectional Streaming


```python import asyncio, json from fastapi import WebSocket

class ChatWebSocket: """Bidirectional streaming chat with WebSocket""" def init(self, model, tokenizer): self.model = model self.tokenizer = tokenizer

async def handle_connection(self, websocket: WebSocket): await websocket.accept() try: while True: data = await websocket.receive_json() prompt = data.get("prompt", "") max_tokens = data.get("max_tokens", 256) # Send status update await websocket.send_json({"event": "start", "prompt_tokens": len(prompt)}) # Stream tokens input_ids = self.tokenizer(prompt, return_tensors="pt").input_ids.to("cuda") generated = 0 for _ in range(max_tokens): logits = self.model(input_ids)[:, -1, :] next_tok = logits.argmax(dim=-1, keepdim=True) token_text = self.tokenizer.decode(next_tok[0]) await websocket.send_json({ "event": "token", "token": token_text, }) input_ids = torch.cat([input_ids, next_tok], dim=-1) generated += 1 if next_tok.item() == self.tokenizer.eos_token_id: break await websocket.send_json({ "event": "done", "total_tokens": generated, }) except Exception as e: await websocket.send_json({"event": "error", "message": str(e)})





Client side


async def stream_client(): import aiohttp async with aiohttp.ClientSession() as session: async with session.ws_connect("ws://localhost:8000/ws/chat") as ws: await ws.send_json({"prompt": "Tell me a story", "max_tokens": 100})

async for msg in ws: data = msg.json() if data["event"] == "token": print(data["token"], end="", flush=True) elif data["event"] == "done": break

```





33. Data Poisoning Defense & Dataset Integrity


33.1 Poisoning Detection Methods


```python





poisoning_detection.py


class DataPoisonDetector: """Detect and filter poisoned/backdoor data in training sets""" def init(self, model, tokenizer, clean_reference_data=None): self.model = model self.tokenizer = tokenizer self.clean_ref = clean_reference_data

def activation_anomaly_detection(self, dataset, layer_idx=-1): """Detect poisoned samples by analyzing internal activations""" self.model.eval() anomalies = [] with torch.no_grad(): for i, sample in enumerate(dataset): input_ids = self.tokenizer(sample["text"], return_tensors="pt").input_ids.to("cuda") # Get activations at specified layer hidden = self.model.embed_tokens(input_ids) cos, sin = self.model.rotary_emb(input_ids, input_ids.shape[1]) for j, layer in enumerate(self.model.layers): hidden = layer(hidden, cos, sin) if j == layer_idx: activations = hidden.mean(dim=1).cpu().numpy() break # Compare to distribution of clean activations if self.clean_ref is not None: distance = np.linalg.norm(activations - self.clean_ref.mean(axis=0)) if distance > self.clean_ref.std(axis=0).mean() * 3: # 3-sigma anomalies.append((i, distance)) return sorted(anomalies, key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True) def perplexity_outlier_detection(self, dataset): """Flag samples with unusually high or low perplexity""" perplexities = [] for i, sample in enumerate(dataset): input_ids = self.tokenizer(sample["text"], return_tensors="pt").input_ids.to("cuda") with torch.no_grad(): logits = self.model(input_ids) loss = F.cross_entropy(logits.view(-1, logits.size(-1)), input_ids.view(-1)) ppl = torch.exp(loss).item() perplexities.append((i, ppl)) # IQR-based outlier detection ppl_values = [p for _, p in perplexities] q1, q3 = np.percentile(ppl_values, [25, 75]) iqr = q3 - q1 lower_bound = q1 - 1.5 * iqr upper_bound = q3 + 1.5 * iqr outliers = [(i, p) for i, p in perplexities if p < lower_bound or p > upper_bound] return outliers def embedding_space_analysis(self, dataset, embedder=None): """Detect clusters of similar samples (potential poisoning campaigns)""" if embedder is None: embedder = self.model embeddings = [] for sample in dataset: input_ids = self.tokenizer(sample["text"], return_tensors="pt").input_ids.to("cuda") with torch.no_grad(): emb = embedder(input_ids).mean(dim=0).cpu().numpy() embeddings.append(emb) embeddings = np.array(embeddings) # DBSCAN clustering to find dense clusters from sklearn.cluster import DBSCAN clustering = DBSCAN(eps=0.3, min_samples=5, metric="cosine").fit(embeddings) cluster_sizes = {} for i, label in enumerate(clustering.labels_): if label != -1: # Not noise cluster_sizes[label] = cluster_sizes.get(label, 0) + 1 # Small dense clusters may indicate coordinated poisoning suspicious_clusters = {k: v for k, v in cluster_sizes.items() if v < 10} return suspicious_clusters

```





33.2 Data Sanitization Pipeline


```python class DataSanitizer: """Sanitize training data against common attacks""" def init(self): self.pii_patterns = [ r"\b\d{3}-\d{2}-\d{4}\b", # SSN r"\b\d{16}\b", # Credit card r"\b[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+.[A-Z|a-z]{2,}\b", # Email r"\b\d{3}[-.]?\d{3}[-.]?\d{4}\b", # Phone ]

def remove_pii(self, text: str) -> str: """Remove personally identifiable information""" import re for pattern in self.pii_patterns: text = re.sub(pattern, "[REDACTED]", text) return text def remove_urls(self, text: str) -> str: """Remove URLs (potential injection vectors)""" import re return re.sub(r"https?://\S+", "[URL]", text) def remove_control_characters(self, text: str) -> str: """Strip Unicode control chars and zero-width characters""" import unicodedata return "".join(c for c in text if unicodedata.category(c) not in ["Cc", "Cf"]) def sanitize_dataset(self, dataset): """Apply all sanitization steps to a dataset""" sanitized = [] for sample in dataset: text = sample["text"] text = self.remove_pii(text) text = self.remove_urls(text) text = self.remove_control_characters(text) # Additional sanitization text = text.replace("\x00", "") # Null bytes sample["text"] = text sanitized.append(sample) return sanitized

```





33.3 Training Integrity Verification


```python class TrainingIntegrity: """Verify training process hasn't been compromised""" def init(self, model): self.model = model self.baseline_gradients = {} self.baseline_losses = []

def capture_gradient_stats(self): """Capture gradient statistics as a fingerprint""" stats = {} for name, param in self.model.named_parameters(): if param.grad is not None: stats[name] = { "mean": param.grad.mean().item(), "std": param.grad.std().item(), "norm": param.grad.norm().item(), } return stats def detect_gradient_anomaly(self, current_grad_stats): """Detect anomalous gradient patterns (backdoor injection)""" if not self.baseline_gradients: return False anomalies = [] for name, stats in current_grad_stats.items(): if name in self.baseline_gradients: baseline = self.baseline_gradients[name] # Check for sudden large changes norm_change = abs(stats["norm"] - baseline["norm"]) / max(baseline["norm"], 1e-8) if norm_change > 10: # 10x change anomalies.append(name) return len(anomalies) > 3 # Multiple anomalous layers def compute_data_influence(self, dataloader): """Estimate influence of each training sample on model behavior""" influences = [] for batch in dataloader: input_ids = batch["input_ids"].to("cuda") # Influence = gradient dot product self.model.zero_grad() loss = self.model(input_ids) loss.backward() # Compute per-sample gradient norm per_sample_influence = 0 for param in self.model.parameters(): if param.grad is not None: per_sample_influence += (param.grad ** 2).sum().item() influences.append(per_sample_influence) return influences





Verify checkpoint hasn't been tampered with


def sign_checkpoint(model_path, secret_key): """Cryptographic signing of model checkpoints""" import hashlib, hmac

# Read model file with open(f"{model_path}/pytorch_model.bin", "rb") as f: model_bytes = f.read() # Create signature signature = hmac.new( secret_key.encode(), model_bytes, hashlib.sha256, ).hexdigest() # Store signature with open(f"{model_path}/signature.txt", "w") as f: f.write(signature)

def verify_checkpoint(model_path, secret_key): """Verify checkpoint hasn't been modified""" import hashlib, hmac

with open(f"{model_path}/pytorch_model.bin", "rb") as f: model_bytes = f.read() with open(f"{model_path}/signature.txt") as f: stored_signature = f.read().strip() expected = hmac.new( secret_key.encode(), model_bytes, hashlib.sha256, ).hexdigest() return hmac.compare_digest(expected, stored_signature)

```





34. Cross-Lingual & Multilingual Training


34.1 Multilingual Tokenization


```python





multilingual_tokenizer.py


class MultilingualTokenizer: """Strategies for handling multiple languages efficiently""" def init(self, base_tokenizer, lang_vocab_boost=None): self.tokenizer = base_tokenizer self.lang_vocab_boost = lang_vocab_boost or {}

def analyze_language_coverage(self, corpus, languages): """Analyze how well the tokenizer covers each language""" coverage = {} for lang in languages: samples = corpus.get(lang, []) if not samples: continue oov_rates = [] compression_ratios = [] for sample in samples[:1000]: tokens = self.tokenizer.tokenize(sample) ids = self.tokenizer.encode(sample) # OOV rate (tokens mapped to <unk>) oov = sum(1 for t in tokens if t == self.tokenizer.unk_token) oov_rates.append(oov / max(len(tokens), 1)) # Compression ratio (bytes per token) compression = len(sample.encode()) / len(ids) compression_ratios.append(compression) coverage[lang] = { "oov_rate": np.mean(oov_rates), "compression_ratio": np.mean(compression_ratios), "sample_count": len(samples), } return coverage def extend_vocabulary(self, new_tokens: list): """Extend tokenizer vocabulary for better language coverage""" current_vocab = self.tokenizer.get_vocab() new_vocab_size = len(current_vocab) + len(new_tokens) # Add new tokens self.tokenizer.add_tokens(new_tokens) print(f"Extended vocab from {len(current_vocab)} to {new_vocab_size}") return new_vocab_size





Example: check or extend tokenizer


from transformers import AutoTokenizer tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("mistralai/Mistral-7B-v0.1")

analyzer = MultilingualTokenizer(tok) coverage = analyzer.analyze_language_coverage( corpus={"zh": chinese_texts, "ar": arabic_texts, "en": english_texts}, languages=["zh", "ar", "en"], ) ```





34.2 Language-Balanced Data Mixing


```python class MultilingualDataMixer: """Mix data from multiple languages with controlled proportions""" def init(self): self.language_datasets = {} # lang -> dataset self.weights = {}

def set_proportions(self, proportions: dict): """Set target language proportions (should sum to 1)""" total = sum(proportions.values()) self.weights = {k: v / total for k, v in proportions.items()} def sample_batch(self, batch_size: int): """Sample a batch respecting language proportions""" batch = [] for lang, weight in self.weights.items(): n_samples = max(1, int(batch_size * weight)) if lang in self.language_datasets: samples = random.choices(self.language_datasets[lang], k=n_samples) batch.extend(samples) random.shuffle(batch) return batch[:batch_size] def upsample_low_resource(self, target_samples: int, min_proportion: float = 0.05): """Upsample low-resource languages to prevent under-training""" for lang, dataset in self.language_datasets.items(): current = len(dataset) if current < target_samples * min_proportion: # Oversample multiplier = int((target_samples * min_proportion) / current) + 1 self.language_datasets[lang] = dataset * multiplier print(f"Upsampled {lang}: {current} -> {len(dataset) * multiplier}")

```





34.3 Cross-Lingual Transfer Learning


```python class CrossLingualTransfer: """Fine-tune on high-resource language, transfer to low-resource""" def init(self, model, tokenizer): self.model = model self.tokenizer = tokenizer

def zero_shot_transfer(self, source_lang_data, target_lang_prompts): """Test cross-lingual transfer without target training""" # Fine-tune on source language # (not shown - standard SFT) # Test on target language results = {} for lang, prompts in target_lang_prompts.items(): acc = self.evaluate(prompts) results[lang] = acc return results def train_on_translated_data(self, source_data, translate_fn, target_lang): """Train on machine-translated data for target language""" translated = [] for sample in source_data: translated_sample = { "prompt": translate_fn(sample["prompt"], target_lang), "response": translate_fn(sample["response"], target_lang), } translated.append(translated_sample) return translated def code_switched_training(self, data_pairs, switch_probability=0.15): """Train with code-switched data to improve multilingual capability""" import random code_switched = [] for source, target in data_pairs: source_tokens = source.split() switched_tokens = [] for token in source_tokens: if random.random() < switch_probability and target: # Replace with translation replacement = target.pop(0) switched_tokens.append(replacement) else: switched_tokens.append(token) code_switched.append(" ".join(switched_tokens)) return code_switched

```





34.4 Multilingual Evaluation


```python class MultilingualEval: """Evaluate model across multiple languages""" def init(self, model, tokenizer): self.model = model self.tokenizer = tokenizer

def evaluate_translation_quality(self, source_texts, target_texts, source_lang, target_lang): """BLEU and COMET evaluation for translation""" from datasets import load_metric # BLEU bleu = load_metric("bleu") predictions = [] for src in source_texts: inputs = self.tokenizer(src, return_tensors="pt").to("cuda") outputs = self.model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=256) pred = self.tokenizer.decode(outputs[0], skip_special_tokens=True) predictions.append(pred) bleu_score = bleu.compute(predictions=predictions, references=target_texts) return bleu_score def cross_lingual_benchmark(self, benchmarks): """Run same benchmark across multiple languages""" results = {} for lang, benchmark in benchmarks.items(): acc = self.run_benchmark(benchmark) results[lang] = acc print(f"{lang}: {acc:.2%}") # Cross-lingual gap if "en" in results: gaps = {lang: results["en"] - acc for lang, acc in results.items()} results["gap_vs_en"] = gaps return results

```

35. Synthetic Data Quality Assurance & Self-Play


35.1 Synthetic Data Validation


```python





synthetic_qa.py


class SyntheticDataValidator: """Validate quality and safety of synthetic training data""" def init(self, validator_model=None): self.validator = validator_model # Strong model to judge quality

def check_factual_consistency(self, question, answer, reference=None): """Check if answer is factually consistent with reference""" if reference is None: return {"consistent": True, "score": 1.0} prompt = f"""Question: {question}

Reference: {reference} Answer: {answer}

Is the answer factually consistent with the reference? (yes/no) Score (0-1):""" return self._judge(prompt)

def check_format_correctness(self, answer, expected_format): """Validate output format matches requirements""" if expected_format == "json": import json try: json.loads(answer) return True except: return False elif expected_format == "code": # Check for code blocks return "```" in answer or "def " in answer or "class " in answer return True def check_difficulty(self, question, target_difficulty): """Estimate question difficulty and flag if too easy/hard""" prompt = f"""Rate this question's difficulty from 1 (very easy) to 10 (very hard):

Question: {question} Difficulty:""" result = self._judge(prompt) estimated = float(result.get("score", 5))

return { "estimated": estimated, "target": target_difficulty, "match": abs(estimated - target_difficulty) <= 2, } def _judge(self, prompt): """Simple judge output""" if self.validator is None: return {"consistent": True, "score": 0.8} inputs = self.validator.tokenizer(prompt, return_tensors="pt").to("cuda") outputs = self.validator.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=50) text = self.validator.tokenizer.decode(outputs[0], skip_special_tokens=True) return {"raw": text, "consistent": "yes" in text.lower()}

class SyntheticDataFilter: """Filter low-quality synthetic samples""" def init(self, quality_threshold=0.7): self.threshold = quality_threshold self.validator = SyntheticDataValidator()

def filter_dataset(self, synthetic_dataset): """Apply multiple quality filters""" kept = [] rejected = {"too_short": 0, "repetitive": 0, "low_quality": 0, "format_error": 0} for sample in synthetic_dataset: text = sample["text"] # Length filter if len(text.split()) < 50: rejected["too_short"] += 1 continue # Repetition filter if self._is_repetitive(text): rejected["repetitive"] += 1 continue # Quality score filter quality = self._quality_score(sample) if quality < self.threshold: rejected["low_quality"] += 1 continue kept.append(sample) print(f"Kept: {len(kept)}, Rejected: {rejected}") return kept def _is_repetitive(self, text: str, ngram=5, threshold=0.3): """Detect repetitive text""" words = text.split() if len(words) < ngram * 2: return False unique_ngrams = set() for i in range(len(words) - ngram + 1): unique_ngrams.add(" ".join(words[i:i+ngram])) repetition_ratio = 1 - len(unique_ngrams) / (len(words) - ngram + 1) return repetition_ratio > threshold def _quality_score(self, sample): """Score synthetic sample quality""" score = 1.0 # Penalize very short responses text = sample.get("text", sample.get("response", "")) if len(text) < 100: score -= 0.2 # Penalize lack of structure if not any(c in text for c in [".", "!", "?"]): score -= 0.1 # Penalize excessive special characters special_ratio = sum(not c.isalnum() and not c.isspace() for c in text) / max(len(text), 1) if special_ratio > 0.3: score -= 0.3 # Penalize URLs if "http" in text: score -= 0.1 return max(0.0, score)

```





35.2 Self-Play Training Pipeline


```python class SelfPlayTrainer: """Train model by playing against itself (AlphaGo-style for LLMs)""" def init(self, model, tokenizer, reward_fn): self.model = model self.tokenizer = tokenizer self.reward_fn = reward_fn self.replay_buffer = []

def generate_opponent_response(self, prompt, temperature=1.0): """Generate a response using current model (acting as opponent)""" inputs = self.tokenizer(prompt, return_tensors="pt").to("cuda") outputs = self.model.generate( **inputs, max_new_tokens=512, do_sample=True, temperature=temperature, ) return self.tokenizer.decode(outputs[0], skip_special_tokens=True) def self_play_round(self, prompts, n_samples=4): """One round of self-play: generate, compare, learn""" round_data = [] for prompt in prompts: # Generate multiple responses responses = [] for _ in range(n_samples): resp = self.generate_opponent_response(prompt, temperature=0.8) responses.append(resp) # Evaluate and rank scored = [] for resp in responses: score = self.reward_fn(prompt, resp) scored.append((resp, score)) scored.sort(key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True) # Best response is "chosen", worst is "rejected" if len(scored) >= 2: round_data.append({ "prompt": prompt, "chosen": scored[0][0], "rejected": scored[-1][0], "chosen_score": scored[0][1], "rejected_score": scored[-1][1], }) # Add to replay buffer self.replay_buffer.extend(round_data) return round_data def train_from_replay(self, batch_size=16): """Train DPO using self-play data""" if len(self.replay_buffer) < batch_size: return batch = random.sample(self.replay_buffer, batch_size) # DPO training step total_loss = 0 for sample in batch: # Compute log probabilities for chosen and rejected # DPO loss: -log(sigma(beta * (log_prob_chosen - log_prob_rejected))) chosen_ids = self.tokenizer(sample["chosen"], return_tensors="pt").input_ids.to("cuda") rejected_ids = self.tokenizer(sample["rejected"], return_tensors="pt").input_ids.to("cuda") chosen_logits = self.model(chosen_ids) rejected_logits = self.model(rejected_ids) # Simplified DPO loss # (full implementation requires reference model log probs) loss = -F.logsigmoid( self.beta * ( chosen_logits.mean() - rejected_logits.mean() ) ).mean() total_loss += loss.item() loss.backward() optimizer.step() optimizer.zero_grad() return total_loss / len(batch)

```





35.3 Iterative Self-Improvement Loop


```python class IterativeSelfImprovement: """Iterative cycle: generate data -> train -> evaluate -> repeat""" def init(self, model, tokenizer, eval_fn, reward_fn): self.model = model self.tokenizer = tokenizer self.eval_fn = eval_fn self.reward_fn = reward_fn self.history = []

def improvement_round(self, prompts, n_generations=64, n_train_steps=100): """One round of self-improvement""" # 1. Generate candidate responses candidates = [] for prompt in prompts: for _ in range(n_generations // len(prompts)): inputs = self.tokenizer(prompt, return_tensors="pt").to("cuda") outputs = self.model.generate(**inputs, max_new_tokens=512, do_sample=True, temperature=0.9) resp = self.tokenizer.decode(outputs[0], skip_special_tokens=True) candidates.append((prompt, resp)) # 2. Filter best candidates using reward model scored = [(p, r, self.reward_fn(p, r)) for p, r in candidates] scored.sort(key=lambda x: x[2], reverse=True) # Keep top 20% as training data top_k = max(1, len(scored) // 5) best = scored[:top_k] # 3. Fine-tune on best responses train_data = [{"prompt": p, "completion": r} for p, r, _ in best] self.sft_train(train_data, steps=n_train_steps) # 4. Evaluate eval_score = self.eval_fn(self.model) self.history.append({ "round": len(self.history) + 1, "eval_score": eval_score, "n_candidates": len(candidates), "kept": len(best), }) return eval_score

```





35.4 Synthetic Data Quality Metrics


Metric Description Target

Diversity Unique n-gram ratio >0.5

Fluency Perplexity under reference model <50

Coherence Next-sentence prediction accuracy >0.7

Factuality Entailment with trusted sources >0.8

Instruction following Format compliance rate >0.95

Safety Non-toxic rate >0.99

Difficulty Question difficulty distribution Matches target

```python def compute_synthetic_data_metrics(generated_dataset, reference_model, tokenizer): """Compute quality metrics for a synthetic dataset""" metrics = {}

# Diversity: unique 4-grams / total 4-grams all_ngrams = set() total_ngrams = 0 for sample in generated_dataset: words = sample["text"].split() for i in range(len(words) - 4 + 1): all_ngrams.add(" ".join(words[i:i+4])) total_ngrams += 1 metrics["diversity"] = len(all_ngrams) / max(total_ngrams, 1) # Fluency: average perplexity perplexities = [] for sample in generated_dataset[:100]: input_ids = tokenizer(sample["text"], return_tensors="pt").input_ids.to("cuda") with torch.no_grad(): loss = reference_model(input_ids) ppl = torch.exp(F.cross_entropy( loss.view(-1, loss.size(-1)), input_ids.view(-1) )).item() perplexities.append(ppl) metrics["avg_perplexity"] = np.mean(perplexities) # Length statistics lengths = [len(s["text"].split()) for s in generated_dataset] metrics["avg_length"] = np.mean(lengths) metrics["std_length"] = np.std(lengths) return metrics

```





36. Model Architecture Search (NAS) & Automated Design


36.1 Neural Architecture Search for LLMs


```python





architecture_search.py


import itertools from dataclasses import dataclass, field from typing import List

@dataclass class ArchConfig: """Configuration for a single architecture candidate""" num_layers: int = 24 hidden_size: int = 2048 num_heads: int = 16 num_kv_heads: int = 4 intermediate_size: int = 5632 # ~2.75 * hidden_size activation: str = "swiglu" norm: str = "rmsnorm" attention_type: str = "gqa" # "mha", "gqa", "mqa", "flash", "mamba" use_moe: bool = False num_experts: int = 0 vocab_size: int = 32000

def param_count(self) -> int: """Estimate parameter count in billions""" vocab = self.vocab_size * self.hidden_size attn_head = self.hidden_size * self.hidden_size * 4 # Q,K,V,O if self.attention_type in ("gqa", "mqa"): kv_ratio = self.num_kv_heads / max(self.num_heads, 1) attn_head = self.hidden_size * self.hidden_size * (2 + 2 * kv_ratio) mlp = 3 * self.hidden_size * self.intermediate_size per_layer = attn_head + mlp if self.use_moe: per_layer = per_layer * self.num_experts * (2 / self.num_experts) # top-2 routing total = vocab + per_layer * self.num_layers + self.hidden_size * self.vocab_size return total / 1e9

class ArchitectureSearcher: """Search over model architecture configurations""" def init(self, target_params: float = 7.0, target_memory: float = 80.0): self.target_params = target_params self.target_memory = target_memory

def generate_search_space(self) -> List[ArchConfig]: """Generate candidate architectures based on scaling laws""" candidates = [] # 7B parameter configurations configs = [ # (layers, hidden, heads, kv_heads, intermed) (32, 4096, 32, 8, 11008), # LLaMA-style (32, 4096, 32, 4, 11008), # Fewer KV heads (40, 4096, 32, 8, 11008), # Deeper (28, 5120, 40, 8, 13824), # Wider (36, 4096, 32, 8, 11008), # Deep + standard (24, 5120, 40, 8, 13824), # Wide + shallow (40, 3584, 28, 4, 9728), # Deep + narrow ] for layers, hidden, heads, kv_heads, intermed in configs: cand = ArchConfig( num_layers=layers, hidden_size=hidden, num_heads=heads, num_kv_heads=kv_heads, intermediate_size=intermed, ) params = cand.param_count() if abs(params - self.target_params) / self.target_params < 0.2: candidates.append(cand) return candidates def score_architecture(self, config: ArchConfig, loss_estimate: float, throughput: float): """Score architecture on efficiency pareto frontier""" params = config.param_count() efficiency = throughput / params # tokens/sec per parameter quality = -loss_estimate * params # Lower loss per param is better return {"efficiency": efficiency, "quality": quality, "combined": efficiency * quality}

```





36.2 Scaling Law Analysis


```python class ScalingLawAnalyzer: """Analyze and predict model performance based on scaling laws""" def init(self): # Chinchilla scaling law coefficients self.a = -0.34 self.b = -0.28 self.e = 1.69 # Irreducible loss

def predict_loss(self, n_params: float, n_tokens: float) -> float: """Predict loss from parameter count and training tokens""" return self.e + self.a * n_params ** (-0.34) + self.b * n_tokens ** (-0.28) def optimal_allocation(self, compute_budget: float) -> dict: """Compute optimal params:tokens ratio for a given compute budget""" # Chinchilla optimal: ~20 tokens per parameter optimal_ratio = 20 # tokens per parameter n_params = (compute_budget / optimal_ratio) ** 0.5 n_tokens = compute_budget / n_params return {"params_b": n_params / 1e9, "tokens_trillion": n_tokens / 1e12} def compute_to_loss_curve(self, n_params: float): """Plot expected loss as training progresses""" tokens = [1e9, 5e9, 1e10, 5e10, 1e11, 5e11, 1e12] losses = [self.predict_loss(n_params, t) for t in tokens] return list(zip(tokens, losses)) def find_isoparams(self, target_loss: float) -> list: """Find (params, tokens) pairs that achieve target loss""" solutions = [] for n_params in [1e8, 3e8, 1e9, 3e9, 1e10, 3e10, 1e11]: # Solve for required tokens n_tokens = (self.b / (target_loss - self.e - self.a * n_params ** (-0.34))) ** (-1/0.28) if n_tokens > 0: solutions.append({ "params_b": n_params / 1e9, "tokens_t": n_tokens / 1e12, "compute": n_params * n_tokens, }) return sorted(solutions, key=lambda x: x["compute"])





Example: optimal allocation for $1M training budget


Assume $10 / A100-hour, ~100 TFLOPS utilization


budget_flops = 1e6 / 10 * 100e12 * 3600 # FLOPs = budget analyzer = ScalingLawAnalyzer() opt = analyzer.optimal_allocation(budget_flops) print(f"Optimal: {opt['params_b']:.1f}B params, {opt['tokens_trillion']:.1f}T tokens") ```





36.3 Ablation Study Management


```python class AblationManager: """Manage and compare architecture ablation experiments""" def init(self, base_config: ArchConfig): self.base = base_config self.results = []

def run_ablations(self): """Run systematic ablations varying one parameter at a time""" ablations = [ ("activation_gelu", {"activation": "gelu"}), ("activation_swiglu", {"activation": "swiglu"}), ("norm_rmsnorm", {"norm": "rmsnorm"}), ("norm_layernorm", {"norm": "layernorm"}), ("gqa_8kv", {"num_kv_heads": 8}), ("gqa_4kv", {"num_kv_heads": 4}), ("mha", {"num_kv_heads": 32, "attention_type": "mha"}), ("moe_8e", {"use_moe": True, "num_experts": 8}), ("moe_16e", {"use_moe": True, "num_experts": 16}), ("narrow_2x", {"intermediate_size": self.base.hidden_size * 2}), ("wide_4x", {"intermediate_size": self.base.hidden_size * 4}), ] for name, overrides in ablations: config = self._apply_overrides(overrides) params = config.param_count() self.results.append({"name": name, "params_b": params, "config": config}) return self.results def _apply_overrides(self, overrides: dict) -> ArchConfig: config_dict = vars(self.base).copy() config_dict.update(overrides) return ArchConfig(**config_dict) def recommend_best_config(self, param_budget: float = 7.0) -> ArchConfig: """Recommend the best config within a parameter budget""" viable = [r for r in self.results if r["params_b"] <= param_budget * 1.1] if not viable: return self.base # Sort by configuration quality (simplified: prefer wider/deeper) viable.sort(key=lambda r: (r["config"].num_layers * r["config"].hidden_size), reverse=True) return viable[0]["config"]

```





36.4 Architecture Decision Guide


Decision Small (<1B) Medium (1B-7B) Large (7B-70B) Very Large (70B+)

Layers 12-16 24-32 32-40 48-80

Hidden dim 768-1024 2048-4096 4096-5120 7168-12288

Heads 12-16 16-32 32-40 48-96

KV heads 4-8 4-8 8 8-16

Intermediate 2048-3072 5632-11008 11008-13824 18944-32768

Activation GELU SwiGLU SwiGLU SwiGLU

Attention MHA GQA GQA GQA + MLA

MoE No No Optional (8-64E) Yes (64-128E)





37. Low-Resource & Edge Deployment


37.1 Model Optimization for Edge


```python





edge_deployment.py


class EdgeModelOptimizer: """Optimize models for deployment on edge/mobile devices""" def init(self, model): self.model = model

def quantize_to_int8(self): """Dynamic quantization for CPU inference""" import torch.quantization quantized = torch.quantization.quantize_dynamic( self.model, {torch.nn.Linear}, # Quantize linear layers dtype=torch.qint8, ) return quantized def fuse_layers(self): """Fuse adjacent layers for faster CPU inference""" import torch.quantization # Fuse Conv + BN + ReLU, or Linear + LayerNorm fused = torch.quantization.fuse_modules( self.model, [["self_attn.q_proj", "self_attn.o_proj"]], # Example fusions ) return fused def prune_to_target(self, target_size_mb: float): """Prune model to fit a target size""" import copy model = copy.deepcopy(self.model) current_size = self._estimate_size_mb(model) sparsity = 1 - (target_size_mb / current_size) # Apply gradual pruning for name, param in model.named_parameters(): if "weight" in name and param.dim() >= 2: threshold = torch.quantile(param.abs(), sparsity) param.data *= (param.abs() > threshold).float() return model def _estimate_size_mb(self, model) -> float: total = sum(p.numel() * p.element_size() for p in model.parameters()) return total / (1024 * 1024) def export_to_onnx(self, output_path="model.onnx"): """Export to ONNX for mobile deployment""" import onnx dummy = torch.randint(0, 100, (1, 128)) torch.onnx.export( self.model, dummy, output_path, input_names=["input_ids"], output_names=["logits"], dynamic_axes={"input_ids": {0: "batch", 1: "seq"}}, opset_version=17, ) print(f"Exported to {output_path}")

```
