37.5 Power Optimization


```python class PowerOptimizer: """Optimize inference for battery-constrained devices""" def init(self, model, batch_size=1): self.model = model self.batch_size = batch_size

def measure_power_usage(self, input_length=128, output_length=64): """Estimate power consumption per inference""" import psutil import time # CPU/GPU power estimation cpu_start = psutil.cpu_percent(interval=None) if torch.cuda.is_available(): gpu_start = torch.cuda.utilization() start = time.time() # Run inference x = torch.randint(0, 1000, (self.batch_size, input_length)).to("cuda") with torch.no_grad(): for _ in range(output_length): logits = self.model(x) next_tok = logits[0, -1].argmax().unsqueeze(0).unsqueeze(0) x = torch.cat([x, next_tok], dim=-1) elapsed = time.time() - start cpu_end = psutil.cpu_percent(interval=None) gpu_end = torch.cuda.utilization() if torch.cuda.is_available() else 0 return { "time_seconds": elapsed, "tokens_per_second": output_length / elapsed, "avg_cpu_percent": (cpu_start + cpu_end) / 2, "avg_gpu_util": (gpu_start + gpu_end) / 2, "estimated_power_watts": (gpu_end / 100) * 300, # Rough GPU power }

```





38. Long Training Run Management & Resilience


38.1 Checkpoint Strategies


```python





training_management.py


import glob, os, json, shutil from dataclasses import dataclass from datetime import datetime

@dataclass class CheckpointStrategy: """Strategy for when and what to save during long training""" save_every_steps: int = 1000 save_every_hours: float = 2.0 keep_last_n: int = 5 save_optimizer: bool = True save_scheduler: bool = True save_on_interrupt: bool = True

def should_save(self, step: int, elapsed_hours: float) -> bool: if step % self.save_every_steps == 0: return True if self.save_every_hours and elapsed_hours % self.save_every_hours < 0.1: return True return False

class CheckpointManager: """Manage checkpoints during long training runs""" def init(self, output_dir="checkpoints", strategy: CheckpointStrategy = None): self.output_dir = output_dir self.strategy = strategy or CheckpointStrategy() self.start_time = datetime.now() os.makedirs(output_dir, exist_ok=True)

def save(self, model, optimizer, scheduler, step, metrics: dict = None): """Save a checkpoint with metadata""" checkpoint_dir = f"{self.output_dir}/step_{step}" os.makedirs(checkpoint_dir, exist_ok=True) # Save model weights torch.save(model.state_dict(), f"{checkpoint_dir}/model.pt") # Save optimizer state if self.strategy.save_optimizer and optimizer: torch.save(optimizer.state_dict(), f"{checkpoint_dir}/optimizer.pt") # Save scheduler state if self.strategy.save_scheduler and scheduler: torch.save(scheduler.state_dict(), f"{checkpoint_dir}/scheduler.pt") # Save metadata metadata = { "step": step, "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat(), "elapsed_hours": (datetime.now() - self.start_time).total_seconds() / 3600, "metrics": metrics or {}, } with open(f"{checkpoint_dir}/metadata.json", "w") as f: json.dump(metadata, f, indent=2) # Prune old checkpoints self._prune_old() print(f"Saved checkpoint at step {step}") def load_latest(self, model, optimizer=None, scheduler=None): """Load the latest checkpoint""" checkpoints = sorted(glob.glob(f"{self.output_dir}/step_*")) if not checkpoints: print("No checkpoint found, starting from scratch") return 0 latest = checkpoints[-1] step = int(latest.split("_")[-1]) model.load_state_dict(torch.load(f"{latest}/model.pt")) if optimizer and os.path.exists(f"{latest}/optimizer.pt"): optimizer.load_state_dict(torch.load(f"{latest}/optimizer.pt")) if scheduler and os.path.exists(f"{latest}/scheduler.pt"): scheduler.load_state_dict(torch.load(f"{latest}/scheduler.pt")) print(f"Resumed from checkpoint at step {step}") return step def _prune_old(self): """Remove old checkpoints, keeping only last N""" checkpoints = sorted(glob.glob(f"{self.output_dir}/step_*")) while len(checkpoints) > self.strategy.keep_last_n: oldest = checkpoints[0] shutil.rmtree(oldest) checkpoints = checkpoints[1:] print(f"Pruned old checkpoint: {oldest}") def save_emergency(self, model, error_msg=""): """Emergency save on training crash""" emergency_dir = f"{self.output_dir}/EMERGENCY_{datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%d_%H%M%S')}" torch.save(model.state_dict(), f"{emergency_dir}.pt") with open(f"{emergency_dir}_error.txt", "w") as f: f.write(error_msg) print(f"Emergency checkpoint saved to {emergency_dir}")

```





38.2 Training Recovery & Automatic Restart


```python class ResilientTrainer: """Training loop with automatic recovery from failures""" def init(self, model, optimizer, scheduler, dataloader, max_restarts=5): self.model = model self.optimizer = optimizer self.scheduler = scheduler self.dataloader = dataloader self.max_restarts = max_restarts self.checkpoint_mgr = CheckpointManager()

def train(self, max_steps=100000): """Training loop with automatic recovery""" for attempt in range(self.max_restarts + 1): try: self._training_loop(max_steps) break # Success except Exception as e: print(f"Training failed (attempt {attempt + 1}): {e}") if attempt < self.max_restarts: print("Restarting from latest checkpoint...") self.model, self.optimizer, self.scheduler = self._recover() else: raise def _training_loop(self, max_steps): """Main training loop with periodic checkpointing""" step = self.checkpoint_mgr.load_latest(self.model, self.optimizer, self.scheduler) self.model.train() data_iter = iter(self.dataloader) while step < max_steps: try: batch = next(data_iter) except StopIteration: data_iter = iter(self.dataloader) batch = next(data_iter) # Training step logits = self.model(batch["input_ids"]) loss = F.cross_entropy(logits.view(-1, logits.size(-1)), batch["labels"].view(-1)) loss.backward() self.optimizer.step() self.scheduler.step() self.optimizer.zero_grad() step += 1 # Checkpoint if step % 1000 == 0: self.checkpoint_mgr.save( self.model, self.optimizer, self.scheduler, step, {"loss": loss.item()}, ) # Health check: detect loss spikes if loss.item() > 100: raise ValueError(f"Loss spike detected: {loss.item()}") def _recover(self): """Recover model state from the latest checkpoint""" self.model, self.optimizer, self.scheduler = self.checkpoint_mgr.load_latest( self.model, self.optimizer, self.scheduler ) return self.model, self.optimizer, self.scheduler

```





38.3 Cloud Spot Instance Management


```python class SpotInstanceManager: """Manage training on preemptible cloud instances""" def init(self, checkpoint_mgr, cloud_provider="aws"): self.checkpoint = checkpoint_mgr self.cloud = cloud_provider

def handle_preemption(self, model, optimizer): """Save and prepare for instance termination""" print("Preemption notice received! Saving checkpoint...") self.checkpoint.save_emergency(model, "Preempted by cloud provider") # Save to persistent storage self._sync_to_cloud() def _sync_to_cloud(self): """Sync checkpoints to cloud storage""" if self.cloud == "aws": import boto3 s3 = boto3.client("s3") for f in glob.glob(f"{self.checkpoint.output_dir}/**"): s3.upload_file(f, "my-bucket", f) elif self.cloud == "gcp": from google.cloud import storage client = storage.Client() bucket = client.bucket("my-bucket") for f in glob.glob(f"{self.checkpoint.output_dir}/**"): blob = bucket.blob(f) blob.upload_from_filename(f) def schedule_checkpoints(self, save_interval_minutes=15): """Periodic checkpointing for spot instances""" import threading def save_loop(): while True: time.sleep(save_interval_minutes * 60) if hasattr(self, "current_model"): self.checkpoint.save(self.current_model, None, None, self.current_step) thread = threading.Thread(target=save_loop, daemon=True) thread.start()

```

def display(self, step, loss, lr, grad_norm, tokens_per_sec, gpu_mem, eta_hours): """Display formatted training status""" import sys status = f"""

39.1 License Compatibility Matrix


```python





licensing.py


class LicenseChecker: """Check license compatibility of training data and model""" LICENSE_CATEGORIES = { "permissive": ["MIT", "Apache-2.0", "BSD-2-Clause", "BSD-3-Clause", "Unlicense", "CC0-1.0"], "weak_copyleft": ["LGPL-2.1", "LGPL-3.0", "MPL-2.0"], "strong_copyleft": ["GPL-2.0", "GPL-3.0", "AGPL-3.0", "CC-BY-SA-4.0"], "non_commercial": ["CC-BY-NC-4.0", "CC-BY-NC-SA-4.0", "CC-BY-NC-ND-4.0"], "unknown": ["Unknown", "Other", ""], }

def __init__(self): self.datasets = {} # dataset_name -> license def register_dataset(self, name: str, license: str, source_url: str = ""): self.datasets[name] = { "license": license, "source_url": source_url, "category": self._categorize(license), } def _categorize(self, license: str) -> str: for category, licenses in self.LICENSE_CATEGORIES.items(): if license in licenses: return category return "unknown" def check_model_license(self, model_license: str, commercial_use: bool = False) -> dict: """Check if training data licenses are compatible with model release""" issues = [] for dataset_name, info in self.datasets.items(): cat = info["category"] if cat == "non_commercial" and commercial_use: issues.append(f"DATASET {dataset_name}: Non-commercial license incompatible with commercial use") elif cat == "strong_copyleft": issues.append(f"DATASET {dataset_name}: Strong copyleft may require open-sourcing model") return { "compatible": len(issues) == 0, "issues": issues, "datasets": self.datasets, } def generate_attribution(self) -> str: """Generate attribution text for model card""" lines = ["## Training Data Attribution", ""] for name, info in self.datasets.items(): lines.append(f"- **{name}**: {info['license']} license") if info["source_url"]: lines.append(f" - Source: {info['source_url']}") return "\n".join(lines)

```





39.2 Model Card Generation


```python class ModelCard: """Generate standardized model cards (HuggingFace format)""" def init(self): self.card = { "model_name": "", "model_description": "", "model_details": {}, "intended_use": "", "factors": "", "metrics": [], "training_data": [], "quantitative_analyses": {}, "ethical_considerations": "", "caveats": "", }

def set_details(self, name: str, description: str, architecture: str, params: int): self.card["model_name"] = name self.card["model_description"] = description self.card["model_details"] = { "architecture": architecture, "parameters": f"{params / 1e9:.1f}B", "context_length": "200K", "license": "Custom", } def add_benchmark(self, name: str, score: float): self.card["metrics"].append({"name": name, "value": score}) def add_training_data(self, name: str, size: str, license: str): self.card["training_data"].append({ "name": name, "size": size, "license": license, }) def generate_model_card(self) -> str: """Generate markdown model card""" lines = [ f"# {self.card['model_name']}", "", self.card["model_description"], "", "## Model Details", "", ] for k, v in self.card["model_details"].items(): lines.append(f"- **{k}**: {v}") lines += ["", "## Intended Use", "", self.card["intended_use"], ""] lines += ["", "## Training Data", ""] for d in self.card["training_data"]: lines.append(f"- **{d['name']}**: {d['size']} ({d['license']})") lines += ["", "## Evaluation Results", ""] for m in self.card["metrics"]: lines.append(f"- **{m['name']}**: {m['value']:.2%}") lines += ["", "## Ethical Considerations", "", self.card["ethical_considerations"], ""] lines += ["", "## Caveats & Recommendations", "", self.card["caveats"], ""] return "\n".join(lines) def save(self, path="README.md"): with open(path, "w") as f: f.write(self.generate_model_card()) print(f"Model card saved to {path}")

```

Does not have factual knowledge beyond training cutoff

Safety filters should be used in production """)

def generate_readme(self) -> str: return "\n".join(self.readme_sections) ```





40.3 Model Release Process


```python class ModelReleasePipeline: """End-to-end process for releasing a model to the community""" def init(self, model_name, model_path, hf_token=None): self.model_name = model_name self.model_path = model_path self.hf_token = hf_token or os.getenv("HF_TOKEN")

def prepare_release(self, benchmarks: dict, model_card_info: dict): """Prepare all release assets""" # 1. Create model card card = ModelCard() card.set_details( name=self.model_name, description=model_card_info["description"], architecture=model_card_info["architecture"], params=model_card_info["params"], ) for bench, score in benchmarks.items(): card.add_benchmark(bench, score) card.save(f"{self.model_path}/README.md") # 2. Create config self._save_config() # 3. Add tokenizer files self._save_tokenizer() print(f"Release assets prepared at {self.model_path}") def upload_to_hub(self, private=False): """Upload model to HuggingFace Hub""" from huggingface_hub import HfApi, create_repo, upload_folder api = HfApi() # Create repo repo_id = f"{api.whoami()['name']}/{self.model_name}" create_repo(repo_id=repo_id, private=private, exist_ok=True) # Upload upload_folder( repo_id=repo_id, folder_path=self.model_path, path_in_repo=".", ignore_patterns=["*.bin", "venv/"], ) print(f"Model uploaded to https://huggingface.co/{repo_id}") return repo_id def add_to_ollama(self): """Create Ollama Modelfile""" modelfile = f"""

FROM {self.model_path}

PARAMETER temperature 0.7 PARAMETER top_p 0.9 PARAMETER num_ctx 131072

TEMPLATE """{{ .Prompt }}""" """ with open(f"{self.model_path}/Modelfile", "w") as f: f.write(modelfile) print(f"Ollama Modelfile created")

def _save_config(self): """Save model config in HuggingFace format""" from transformers import PretrainedConfig config = PretrainedConfig( model_type="llama", hidden_size=4096, num_hidden_layers=32, num_attention_heads=32, num_key_value_heads=8, ) config.save_pretrained(self.model_path) def _save_tokenizer(self): """Save tokenizer files""" import json tokenizer_config = { "bos_token": "<s>", "eos_token": "</s>", "pad_token": "<pad>", "model_max_length": 200000, } with open(f"{self.model_path}/tokenizer_config.json", "w") as f: json.dump(tokenizer_config, f, indent=2)

```

Example: [0, 4, 8, 12, 16] for every 4th layer layers_to_transform=None, # === INITIALIZATION === # LoRA weight initialization: # "default" = Kaiming uniform for A, zeros for B (standard) # "gaussian" = Gaussian for A (experimental) init_lora_weights="default", # 41.6 Model Configuration — Every Architecture Parameter Explained


```python





model_config_annotated.py — Transformer model architecture parameters


from dataclasses import dataclass from typing import Optional

@dataclass class AnnotatedModelConfig: """ Complete Transformer model configuration with field-by-field explanations.

These parameters directly control the model's capability, memory usage, and inference speed. Changing any parameter requires re-training. """ # === VOCABULARY === # Number of unique tokens in the tokenizer vocabulary. # Common values: 32000 (Mistral), 128000 (LLaMA 3), 64000 (DeepSeek) # Larger vocab = more tokens, more parameters, better coverage # Smaller vocab = more compression, faster, less memory vocab_size: int = 32000, # === HIDDEN DIMENSION (d_model) === # The width of the model — the embedding dimension for each token. # This is the primary driver of model capacity. # 512 = Tiny (60M params) # 768 = Small (125M params) # 1024 = Medium (350M params) # 2048 = Moderately large (1.3B params) # 4096 = Large (7B params) # 5120 = Very large (13B params) # 8192 = Extremely large (70B params) # Doubling hidden_size roughly quadruples compute cost hidden_size: int = 4096, # === NUMBER OF LAYERS === # How many transformer blocks to stack. # More layers = deeper model, better at complex reasoning # 8-12 = small models # 24-32 = medium models (1B-7B) # 32-40 = large models (7B-13B) # 48-80 = very large models (30B-70B) # 96+ = frontier models (180B+) # Rule: deeper is better for reasoning, wider is better for memorization num_hidden_layers: int = 32, # === ATTENTION HEADS === # Number of attention heads in the multi-head attention mechanism. # Each head learns different attention patterns. # hidden_size must be divisible by num_attention_heads # Common values: hidden_size / 64 to hidden_size / 128 # 8-12 for small models, 16-32 for medium, 32-96 for large num_attention_heads: int = 32, # === KV HEADS (GROUPED-QUERY ATTENTION) === # Number of key-value heads. Key optimization that reduces KV cache size. # num_attention_heads = full multi-head attention (MHA) # num_key_value_heads = 1 = multi-query attention (MQA) # num_key_value_heads < num_attention_heads = grouped-query attention (GQA) # Fewer KV heads = smaller KV cache, less memory for long context # But may slightly reduce quality for very complex attention patterns # Common: 8 KV heads for 32 query heads (4:1 ratio) num_key_value_heads: int = 8, # === INTERMEDIATE SIZE (FFN) === # The hidden dimension of the feed-forward network in each transformer block. # For SwiGLU: intermediate_size = 8/3 * hidden_size (roughly 2.7x) # For GELU: intermediate_size = 4 * hidden_size # Larger = more capacity per layer, more parameters # Common: hidden_size * 4 (GELU), int(hidden_size * 8/3) (SwiGLU) intermediate_size: int = 11008, # === MAX POSITION EMBEDDINGS === # Maximum sequence length the model was trained on / can handle. # Longer = requires more attention computation (O(n²) w/o FlashAttention) # Longer = requires more KV cache memory # Common: 2048 (older), 8192 (Mistral), 131072 (LLaMA 3), 200000 (custom) max_position_embeddings: int = 200000, # === RoPE THETA === # Base frequency for Rotary Position Embeddings. # Higher theta = better long-context performance (more position resolution) # 10000 = original RoPE (good for 2K context) # 500000 = LLaMA 3 (good for 8K+) # 1000000 = extended (good for 32K+) # 10000000 = aggressive (good for 128K+) rope_theta: float = 1000000.0, # === HIDDEN DROPOUT === # Dropout probability applied to hidden states (after embeddings, before output). # Usually 0.0 for large models (they rely on data diversity) # 0.1-0.2 for small models (helps prevent overfitting) hidden_dropout_prob: float = 0.0, # === ATTENTION DROPOUT === # Dropout applied to attention weights. # Usually 0.0 for pre-training # Can add 0.1 for fine-tuning on very small datasets attention_dropout_prob: float = 0.0, # === NORMALIZATION EPS === # Small constant added to layer normalization denominator. # Prevents division by zero. Standard: 1e-5 or 1e-6 rms_norm_eps: float = 1e-5, # === HEAD DIMENSION === # Dimension of each attention head. Usually hidden_size / num_attention_heads. # Override if you want non-standard head dimensions. head_dim: Optional[int] = None, # === TIED WEIGHTS === # Whether to tie the input embedding and output projection weights. # True = shared weights (saves parameters, helps training) # False = separate weights (slightly more capacity) tie_word_embeddings: bool = True, # === ACTIVATION FUNCTION === # Activation function for the FFN. # "silu" / "swish" = SwiGLU (best for LLMs, needs 3 projection matrices) # "gelu" = GELU (standard, used in older models) # "relu" = ReLU (simple, less common) hidden_act: str = "silu", # === MODEL TYPE === # HuggingFace model architecture identifier. model_type: str = "llama",

) ```





42. Training Pipeline — Fully Annotated Training Loop


This section provides a complete training script where every parameter and step is explained.

```python





fully_annotated_training_loop.py — EVERY line explained


import torch import torch.nn as nn import torch.nn.functional as F from torch.utils.data import DataLoader from torch.optim import AdamW from transformers import get_cosine_schedule_with_warmup from accelerate import Accelerator from datasets import load_from_disk import wandb import math import time import os





──────────────────────────────────────────────


STEP 1: CONFIGURATION


──────────────────────────────────────────────


Model architecture hyperparameters


These determine the model's capacity, memory usage, and speed


VOCAB_SIZE = 32000 # Number of unique tokens in vocabulary # Each token gets an embedding vector of size HIDDEN_SIZE HIDDEN_SIZE = 768 # Width/dimension of each token's representation # Higher = more capacity, more memory, slower NUM_LAYERS = 12 # Number of transformer blocks stacked # Each layer adds capacity for hierarchical reasoning NUM_HEADS = 12 # Attention heads — each learns different relationships # Must divide HIDDEN_SIZE evenly: 768/12 = 64 dim per head NUM_KV_HEADS = 4 # Key-value heads for Grouped Query Attention # Fewer than NUM_HEADS saves KV cache memory # KV cache memory = seq_len * head_dim * num_kv_heads * 2 * num_layers * 2 bytes INTERMEDIATE_SIZE = 2048 # FFN inner dimension (hidden dimension * ~2.67 for SwiGLU) # Larger = more non-linear capacity, more parameters MAX_SEQ_LEN = 8192 # Maximum sequence length the model processes # Attention cost is O(n²) without FlashAttention ROPE_THETA = 500000.0 # RoPE base frequency — higher = better long-range position encoding





Training hyperparameters


These control the optimization dynamics


BATCH_SIZE = 4 # Samples per GPU per step (micro batch) # Smaller = less memory, more steps to converge GRAD_ACCUM = 8 # Gradient accumulation steps # Effective batch = BATCH_SIZE * GRAD_ACCUM * num_gpus # Standard: 256-512 samples effective batch for small models LEARNING_RATE = 3e-4 # Peak learning rate — how much to update weights each step # Too high: loss diverges. Too low: slow convergence. # Standard range: 1e-5 (7B) to 6e-4 (125M) WARMUP_STEPS = 500 # Steps to linearly increase LR from 0 to peak # Helps stabilize early training when weights are random WEIGHT_DECAY = 0.1 # L2 regularization — larger = stronger, prevents overfitting # Common: 0.01-0.1 for LLMs MAX_STEPS = 5000 # Total training steps # More steps = lower loss, but diminishing returns MAX_GRAD_NORM = 1.0 # Gradient clipping threshold # Prevents exploding gradients from causing NaN loss BETAS = (0.9, 0.95) # AdamW optimizer momentum parameters: # beta1 = 0.9: how much to trust the recent gradient direction # beta2 = 0.95: how much to trust the recent gradient magnitude





──────────────────────────────────────────────


STEP 2: INITIALIZE ACCELERATOR


──────────────────────────────────────────────


Accelerator handles:


- Device placement (GPU/CPU automatic)


- Mixed precision (fp16/bf16 automatic)


- Distributed training (DDP/DeepSpeed)


- Gradient accumulation


accelerator = Accelerator( # Mixed precision mode: # "fp16" = float16 (faster, less stable, needs loss scaling) # "bf16" = bfloat16 (fast, very stable, needs Ampere+ GPU) # "no" = float32 (slow, high memory) mixed_precision="bf16",

# Number of gradient accumulation steps # Accelerator handles the accumulation automatically gradient_accumulation_steps=GRAD_ACCUM, # Log with wandb log_with="wandb",

)





──────────────────────────────────────────────


STEP 3: CREATE MODEL


──────────────────────────────────────────────


Import your model architecture


model = TransformerModel( vocab_size=VOCAB_SIZE, # Embedding matrix: [VOCAB_SIZE × HIDDEN_SIZE] hidden_size=HIDDEN_SIZE, # Width of all hidden representations num_layers=NUM_LAYERS, # Depth: number of transformer blocks num_heads=NUM_HEADS, # Attention heads per layer num_kv_heads=NUM_KV_HEAD, # KV heads for GQA (memory savings) intermediate_size=INTERMEDIATE_SIZE, # FFN inner dimension max_position_embeddings=MAX_SEQ_LEN, # Max positions for RoPE rope_theta=ROPE_THETA, # RoPE frequency base )





Log total parameter count


Total parameters = embedding(32K*768)


+ layers * (attention(4768768) + MLP(37682048))


+ lm_head(768*32K)


total_params = sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters()) trainable_params = sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters() if p.requires_grad) accelerator.print(f"Model parameters:") accelerator.print(f" Total: {total_params/1e6:.1f}M ({total_params/1e9:.2f}B)") accelerator.print(f" Trainable: {trainable_params/1e6:.1f}M ({trainable_params/1e9:.2f}B)")





──────────────────────────────────────────────


STEP 4: LOAD DATA


──────────────────────────────────────────────


Load pre-tokenized dataset from disk


The dataset should have "input_ids" and "labels" columns


input_ids: token IDs for the input sequence


labels: token IDs for the target (usually same as input_ids for LM)


dataset = load_from_disk("data/tokenized_dataset")





Create DataLoader — handles batching, shuffling, and multi-process loading


dataloader = DataLoader( dataset, # Number of samples per batch (per GPU) batch_size=BATCH_SIZE, # Shuffle each epoch — prevents the model from learning order patterns shuffle=True, # Number of subprocesses for data loading # Higher = faster data loading, more CPU memory # Good rule: 4-8 per GPU num_workers=4, # Pin memory: faster GPU transfer, uses more system RAM # If you have enough RAM, keep True pin_memory=True, # Drop the last incomplete batch (maintains consistent batch size) drop_last=True, )





──────────────────────────────────────────────


STEP 5: OPTIMIZER & SCHEDULER


──────────────────────────────────────────────


AdamW optimizer — standard for LLM training


Maintains per-parameter learning rates (adaptive)


optimizer = AdamW( model.parameters(), # Peak learning rate — scales the update magnitude lr=LEARNING_RATE, # Weight decay (L2 penalty) applied to non-bias/norm parameters weight_decay=WEIGHT_DECAY, # Adam beta parameters: betas=BETAS, # Small epsilon to prevent division by zero eps=1e-8, )





Cosine learning rate schedule with linear warmup


Phase 1 (warmup): LR goes from 0 → peak over WARMUP_STEPS


Phase 2 (cosine): LR goes from peak → 0 following cosine curve


This is the standard scheduler for LLM training


scheduler = get_cosine_schedule_with_warmup( optimizer, # Steps for warmup — usually 1-10% of total num_warmup_steps=WARMUP_STEPS, # Total training steps — LR reaches 0 at this point num_training_steps=MAX_STEPS, )





──────────────────────────────────────────────


STEP 6: PREPARE WITH ACCELERATOR


──────────────────────────────────────────────


Accelerator.prepare() automatically:


1. Moves model to correct device (GPU/CPU)


2. Wraps model in DDP/FSDP for multi-GPU


3. Wraps optimizer for mixed precision


4. Wraps dataloader for distributed sampling


5. Replaces scheduler for correct step counting


model, optimizer, dataloader, scheduler = accelerator.prepare( model, optimizer, dataloader, scheduler )





──────────────────────────────────────────────


STEP 7: WANDB LOGGING


──────────────────────────────────────────────


Initialize Weights & Biases for experiment tracking


if accelerator.is_main_process: wandb.init( project="wfb-model", config={ "vocab_size": VOCAB_SIZE, "hidden_size": HIDDEN_SIZE, "num_layers": NUM_LAYERS, "batch_size": BATCH_SIZE, "grad_accum": GRAD_ACCUM, "effective_batch": BATCH_SIZE * GRAD_ACCUM * accelerator.num_processes, "learning_rate": LEARNING_RATE, "warmup_steps": WARMUP_STEPS, "parameters_b": total_params / 1e9, }, )





──────────────────────────────────────────────


STEP 8: TRAINING LOOP


──────────────────────────────────────────────


accelerator.print("Starting training...") model.train() global_step = 0 total_loss = 0.0 start_time = time.time()





Main training loop — runs until MAX_STEPS


while global_step < MAX_STEPS: for batch in dataloader: # ── Forward pass ── # input_ids: tensor of shape (batch_size, seq_len) # labels: tensor of shape (batch_size, seq_len) — usually same as input_ids input_ids = batch["input_ids"] labels = batch["labels"] if "labels" in batch else input_ids.clone()

# Forward pass through the model # Returns logits: (batch_size, seq_len, vocab_size) # Each position predicts the probability distribution for the next token logits = model(input_ids) # ── Loss computation ── # Cross-entropy loss: compares predicted logits to actual labels # We ignore the padding token ID (0) in the loss computation # shift_logits: take all positions except the last # shift_labels: take all positions except the first # (the model predicts token N+1 from token N) loss = F.cross_entropy( logits.view(-1, logits.size(-1)), # (batch*seq, vocab) — flatten batch+seq labels.view(-1), # (batch*seq,) — flattened labels ignore_index=0, # Don't compute loss for padding tokens ) # ── Backward pass (automatic gradient computation) ── # accelerator.backward() handles: # - Scaled loss for gradient accumulation # - Mixed precision scaling accelerator.backward(loss) # ── Gradient clipping (if sync point) ── # Scale gradients down if their norm exceeds MAX_GRAD_NORM # Prevents single large gradient from destabilizing training if accelerator.sync_gradients: accelerator.clip_grad_norm_(model.parameters(), MAX_GRAD_NORM) # ── Optimizer step ── # Update model weights using computed gradients optimizer.step() # Update learning rate scheduler scheduler.step() # Reset gradients to zero for next step optimizer.zero_grad() # ── Logging ── total_loss += loss.item() global_step += 1 if global_step % 100 == 0: avg_loss = total_loss / 100 current_lr = scheduler.get_last_lr()[0] elapsed = time.time() - start_time tokens_per_sec = (BATCH_SIZE * MAX_SEQ_LEN * global_step) / elapsed if accelerator.is_main_process: accelerator.print( f"Step {global_step}/{MAX_STEPS} | " f"Loss: {avg_loss:.4f} | " f"LR: {current_lr:.2e} | " f"Tokens/s: {tokens_per_sec:.0f} | " f"ETA: {(MAX_STEPS - global_step) * elapsed / max(global_step, 1) / 3600:.1f}h" ) wandb.log({ "loss": avg_loss, "learning_rate": current_lr, "tokens_per_second": tokens_per_sec, "step": global_step, }) total_loss = 0.0 # ── Checkpoint saving ── if global_step % 1000 == 0: accelerator.save_state(f"checkpoints/step_{global_step}") accelerator.print(f"Saved checkpoint at step {global_step}") # ── Termination condition ── if global_step >= MAX_STEPS: break





──────────────────────────────────────────────


STEP 9: SAVE FINAL MODEL


──────────────────────────────────────────────


accelerator.save_state("checkpoints/final") accelerator.print(f"Training complete! Total time: {(time.time() - start_time) / 3600:.1f}h")

if accelerator.is_main_process: wandb.finish() ```





43. Data Processing Pipeline — Fully Annotated


This section provides a complete data processing script where every parameter and transformation is explained.

```python





fully_annotated_data_pipeline.py — EVERY line explained


import multiprocessing as mp from datasets import load_dataset, load_from_disk, concatenate_datasets from transformers import AutoTokenizer import numpy as np from tqdm import tqdm





──────────────────────────────────────────────


KEY DATASET PARAMETERS EXPLAINED


──────────────────────────────────────────────


Dataset size: how many tokens to train on


Chinchilla optimal: ~20 tokens per parameter


For a 125M model: ~2.5B tokens


For a 7B model: ~140B tokens


For a 70B model: ~1.4T tokens


Streaming vs download:


streaming=True: read data on-the-fly, no disk space needed


streaming=False: download entire dataset (needs TB of space)


Number of shards:


Splits the dataset into N parts for parallel processing


More shards = more parallel files, faster loading


Recommended: num_shards = number of CPU cores


TARGET_TOKENS = 2_500_000_000 # 2.5B tokens for a 125M model MAX_SEQ_LENGTH = 2048 # Tokenize to this many tokens per sample VOCAB_SIZE = 32000 # Tokenizer vocabulary size NUM_PROC = mp.cpu_count() # Use all CPU cores for parallel processing





──────────────────────────────────────────────


STEP 1: LOAD TOKENIZER


──────────────────────────────────────────────


A tokenizer converts raw text into token IDs.


Key properties:


vocab_size: number of unique tokens (32K-128K)


bos_token: beginning of sequence marker ()





eos_token: end of sequence marker ()


pad_token: padding token (, used for batching)


unk_token: unknown token (, for characters not in vocab)


You have two options:


Option A: Use a pre-trained tokenizer (recommended for most cases)


tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained("mistralai/Mistral-7B-v0.1")





Option B: Train your own tokenizer (for domain-specific data)


from tokenizers import Tokenizer, models, trainers


tokenizer = Tokenizer(models.BPE())


trainer = trainers.BpeTrainer(vocab_size=32000)


tokenizer.train_from_iterator(text_iterator, trainer=trainer)


Set padding token — some tokenizers don't have one by default


We use the EOS token as padding (common practice for autoregressive models)


tokenizer.pad_token = tokenizer.eos_token





Print tokenizer info


print(f"Tokenizer: {tokenizer.class.name}") print(f" Vocab size: {tokenizer.vocab_size}") print(f" Max length: {tokenizer.model_max_length}") print(f" Special tokens: {tokenizer.special_tokens_map}")





──────────────────────────────────────────────


STEP 2: LOAD DATASET


──────────────────────────────────────────────


Dataset options explained:


"HuggingFaceFW/fineweb" — cleaned web text (15T tokens, high quality)


"tiiuae/falcon-refinedweb" — web text (600B tokens)


"codeparrot/github-code" — source code (200GB)


"bigcode/the-stack" — source code (6TB)


"openwebmath" — math content


"c4" — Colossal Clean Crawled Corpus


dataset = load_dataset( "HuggingFaceFW/fineweb", # Dataset split: "train", "validation", or "test" split="train", # Streaming mode: loads data on-demand without downloading full dataset # True = no disk space, slower repeated access # False = full download, faster subsequent access streaming=True, # Subset/sample selection (if the dataset has multiple configs) # "default" = standard configuration name="default", )





──────────────────────────────────────────────


STEP 3: FILTER AND SAMPLE


──────────────────────────────────────────────


Apply quality filters to remove low-quality data


def quality_filter(example): """Filter out low-quality text samples.

Each filter returns a boolean (True = keep, False = discard). Key/value explanations: "text": the raw text content of the sample (string) len(example["text"]): character length of the text """ text = example["text"] # Minimum text length (in characters) # Shorter texts often contain: boilerplate, error messages, single words # Minimum: 200 chars (~50 tokens, reasonable minimum) if len(text) < 200: return False # Maximum text length (in characters) # Very long texts may be concatenated documents or logs # Maximum: 100000 chars (~25K tokens, chunking will split further) if len(text) > 100000: return False # Mean word length — detects non-linguistic content words = text.split() if words: mean_word_len = sum(len(w) for w in words) / len(words) # Very short words (<3): often non-English or tokenization artifacts # Very long words (>10): often code, math, or concatenated strings if mean_word_len < 3 or mean_word_len > 10: return False # Line uniqueness ratio — detects repetitive/ templated content # Common in: log files, boilerplate HTML, spam lines = text.split("\n") if lines: unique_lines = len(set(lines)) unique_ratio = unique_lines / len(lines) # Low unique ratio (<0.3) = highly repetitive content if unique_ratio < 0.3: return False # Bullet/list character ratio — detects content that's mostly formatting # Common in: data dumps, markdown-heavy pages, listicles bullet_count = text.count("*") + text.count("-") + text.count("#") if bullet_count / max(len(text), 1) > 0.1: return False return True





Apply filter to the streaming dataset


filter() processes data lazily (only when iterated)


dataset = dataset.filter(quality_filter)





Take only enough samples to reach target tokens


Each sample averages ~1000 tokens after tokenization


So for 2.5B tokens, we need ~2.5M samples


num_samples_needed = TARGET_TOKENS // (MAX_SEQ_LENGTH * 0.8) # 80% utilization dataset = dataset.take(num_samples_needed)





──────────────────────────────────────────────


STEP 4: TOKENIZATION FUNCTION


──────────────────────────────────────────────


def tokenize_function(examples): """Convert raw text to token IDs.

Parameters (in the 'examples' dict): "text" (list of strings): batch of raw text samples Returns: dict with "input_ids" (list of lists of token IDs) Key tokenizer parameters: truncation: whether to truncate sequences longer than max_length max_length: maximum number of tokens per sequence padding: whether to pad sequences to equal length (False for training) """ # The tokenizer converts text to integer IDs: # "Hello, world!" → [1, 15043, 29892, 31822, 2] # Where: 1 = <s> (BOS), 15043="Hello", 29892=",", 31822="world", 2 = </s> return tokenizer( # List of texts to tokenize examples["text"], # Truncate sequences longer than MAX_SEQ_LENGTH # Prevents memory issues from very long sequences truncation=True, # Maximum number of tokens per sequence # Longer sequences = more context but more memory max_length=MAX_SEQ_LENGTH, # Don't pad — let the collator handle batch padding # Saves storage space and compute padding=False, # Return PyTorch tensors (instead of lists) return_tensors=None, # Returns lists (faster for dataset processing) )





Apply tokenization in parallel (uses multiple CPU cores)


This is the slowest step in the pipeline — parallelism is critical


dataset = dataset.map( tokenize_function, # Process in batches (more efficient than one-at-a-time) batched=True, # Remove the raw "text" column after tokenization (saves memory) remove_columns=["text"], # Number of parallel processes # More = faster, but uses more RAM # Rule: num_proc = number of CPU cores (12-64 typical) num_proc=NUM_PROC, )





──────────────────────────────────────────────


STEP 5: FILTER BY SEQUENCE LENGTH


──────────────────────────────────────────────


Remove sequences that are too short (after tokenization)


These have very few training signal and waste compute


def filter_short_sequences(example): """Keep only sequences above minimum token length.

"input_ids": list of token IDs for this sample """ # Minimum: 64 tokens # Shorter sequences: little training signal, cause padding inefficiency return len(example["input_ids"]) >= 64

dataset = dataset.filter(filter_short_sequences)





──────────────────────────────────────────────


STEP 6: SHARD AND SAVE


──────────────────────────────────────────────


Save to disk in shards (multiple files) for faster loading


More shards = more parallel I/O during training


output_path = "data/tokenized_dataset" num_shards = 64





Create output directory


import os os.makedirs(output_path, exist_ok=True)





Save shards


dataset.save_to_disk( output_path, num_shards=num_shards, )

print(f"Dataset saved to {output_path}") print(f" Number of shards: {num_shards}") print(f" Number of samples: {dataset.dataset_size if hasattr(dataset, 'dataset_size') else 'streaming'}")





──────────────────────────────────────────────


STEP 7: VERIFY DATASET


──────────────────────────────────────────────


Load a small sample to verify


import torch from torch.utils.data import DataLoader

verify_dataset = load_from_disk(output_path) verify_loader = DataLoader(verify_dataset, batch_size=2, shuffle=True) sample = next(iter(verify_loader))

print(f"\nVerification:") print(f" Total samples: {len(verify_dataset)}") print(f" Example input_ids shape: {sample['input_ids'].shape}") print(f" Example input_ids: {sample['input_ids'][0][:20]}...") print(f" Decoded sample: {tokenizer.decode(sample['input_ids'][0][:50])}")





Each sample contains:


"input_ids": (seq_len,) — token IDs for model input


Labels are created during training by shifting input_ids


(The model predicts token[i+1] from token[i])


```

44.1 vLLM Server Configuration — Annotated


```python





vllm_server_annotated.py — vLLM inference server with field explanations


from vllm import LLM, SamplingParams from vllm.engine.arg_utils import AsyncEngineArgs





──────────────────────────────────────────────


ENGINE ARGUMENTS — Model Loading Configuration


──────────────────────────────────────────────


engine_args = AsyncEngineArgs( # === MODEL PATH === # Path to model checkpoint or HuggingFace model ID # Can be local path or HF repo like "mistralai/Mistral-7B-v0.1" model="./checkpoints/final",

# === TOKENIZER === # Path to tokenizer (defaults to model path if not specified) tokenizer="./checkpoints/final", # === TENSOR PARALLEL SIZE === # Number of GPUs to split the model across. # For tensor parallelism: model is split layer-by-layer across GPUs. # 1 = single GPU (no tensor parallelism) # 2 = split across 2 GPUs (each holds half of each layer) # 4 = split across 4 GPUs # Higher = more memory available, more inter-GPU communication # Rule of thumb: use tensor_parallel_size for models larger than 1 GPU can hold tensor_parallel_size=1, # === PIPELINE PARALLEL SIZE === # Number of pipeline stages (split layers across GPUs). # Different from tensor parallelism: layers are split, not sharded. # Typically used for very large models (>70B) across multiple nodes. pipeline_parallel_size=1, # === MAX MODEL LEN === # Maximum sequence length the model can handle. # This determines the KV cache size. # Each token requires: 2 * num_layers * num_heads * head_dim * 2 bytes # For a 7B model: ~2MB per token of KV cache # 200000 tokens: ~400GB (needs 8x A100 with 80GB) max_model_len=200000, # === GPU MEMORY UTILIZATION === # Fraction of GPU memory to use for the model (0.0-1.0). # Higher = more memory for KV cache, less room for other things # 0.95 = standard (leaves 5% for internal operations) # 0.90 = safer (if you get OOM errors) gpu_memory_utilization=0.95, # === QUANTIZATION === # Weight quantization method: # None = FP16 (full precision) # "awq" = Activation-Aware Weight Quantization (4-bit) # "gptq" = GPTQ quantization (4-bit) # "fp8" = FP8 quantization (H100/Blackwell) quantization=None, # === KV CACHE DTYPE === # Data type for KV cache: # "auto" = same as model dtype # "fp8" = FP8 KV cache (saves 50% memory, H100/Blackwell only) kv_cache_dtype="auto", # === SEED === # Random seed for reproducibility seed=42, # === TRUST REMOTE CODE === # Whether to trust custom code in HuggingFace configs. # Only enable for trusted model sources. trust_remote_code=False, # === ENFORCE EAGER === # Disable CUDA graph optimization (debugging only). # True = slower but easier to debug # False = use CUDA graphs for speed enforce_eager=False, # === MAX NUM SEQS === # Maximum number of sequences that can be processed concurrently. # Higher = more concurrent requests, more memory. max_num_seqs=256, # === MAX NUM BATCHED TOKENS === # Maximum number of tokens per batch across all sequences. # Higher = larger batches, higher throughput, more memory. max_num_batched_tokens=8192, # === DISABLE LOG STATS === # Suppress logging of statistics. disable_log_stats=False,

)





──────────────────────────────────────────────


SAMPLING PARAMETERS — Generation Configuration


──────────────────────────────────────────────


sampling_params = SamplingParams( # === TEMPERATURE === # Controls randomness: lower = more deterministic # 0.0 = greedy (always pick highest probability token) # 0.7 = good default for chat # 1.0 = maximum randomness (creative) temperature=0.7,

# === TOP-P (NUCLEUS SAMPLING) === # Cumulative probability cutoff for token selection # 1.0 = consider all tokens (disabled) # 0.9 = tokens comprising 90% of probability mass # 0.5 = very focused (only high-probability tokens) top_p=0.9, # === TOP-K === # Number of highest probability tokens to consider # -1 = consider all tokens (disabled) # 50 = only the top 50 tokens by probability # 10 = very focused (only top 10 tokens) top_k=50, # === MAX TOKENS === # Maximum number of tokens to generate max_tokens=4096, # === STOP TOKENS === # List of token IDs or strings that stop generation stop=["</s>", "<|im_end|>"], # === PRESENCE PENALTY === # Penalty for tokens that have appeared at least once # Positive = discourage repetition, encourage new topics # Range: -2.0 to 2.0 presence_penalty=0.0, # === FREQUENCY PENALTY === # Penalty proportional to token frequency in output # Positive = discourage high-frequency tokens # Range: -2.0 to 2.0 frequency_penalty=0.0, # === REPETITION PENALTY === # Penalty for tokens that have already appeared # 1.0 = no penalty # 1.1 = mild penalty # 1.2 = moderate penalty (reduces loops) repetition_penalty=1.0, # === BEST OF === # Generate N sequences, return the best one (by highest log probability) # 1 = just generate once # >1 = best-of-N sampling (more compute, better quality) best_of=1, # === USE BEAM SEARCH === # Whether to use beam search instead of sampling use_beam_search=False, # === SKIP SPECIAL TOKENS === # Whether to skip special tokens in the output skip_special_tokens=True, # === SPACE BETWEEN SPECIAL TOKENS === # Add spaces before/after special tokens spaces_between_special_tokens=True, # === STOP TOKEN IDS === # Token IDs that stop generation (in addition to EOS) stop_token_ids=[],

)





──────────────────────────────────────────────


CREATE ENGINE AND GENERATE


──────────────────────────────────────────────


Initialize the LLM engine


llm = LLM( model=engine_args.model, tokenizer=engine_args.tokenizer, tensor_parallel_size=engine_args.tensor_parallel_size, max_model_len=engine_args.max_model_len, gpu_memory_utilization=engine_args.gpu_memory_utilization, quantization=engine_args.quantization, )





Generate


outputs = llm.generate( ["Explain how transformers work."],

sampling_params=sampling_params,

)

for output in outputs: prompt = output.prompt generated_text = output.outputs[0].text print(f"Generated: {generated_text}") ```

from prometheus_client import Counter, Histogram, Gauge, Summary import time import psutil import torch





=============================================================================


PROMETHEUS METRICS — Every metric explained


=============================================================================


COUNTER — cumulative count that only increases


Used for: total requests, total tokens, total errors


Total inference requests received since server started


Use: track overall usage volume, detect traffic spikes


TOTAL_REQUESTS = Counter( "llm_requests_total", # Metric name (snake_case) "Total number of inference requests received", # Help text (description) )





Total tokens generated across all requests


Use: compute cost, track usage patterns

Total requests that resulted in errors (timeout, OOM, etc.)


Use: monitor error rate, alert on sudden increases

HISTOGRAM — distribution of values over configurable buckets


Used for: latency, batch sizes, generation lengths


Request latency (end-to-end time from receive to complete response)


Buckets: 100ms to 120s — covers typical LLM inference range


LATENCY_HISTOGRAM = Histogram( "llm_latency_seconds", "Request latency distribution in seconds", # Bucket boundaries (in seconds): # For chat: p50 ~0.5s, p95 ~5s, p99 ~15s buckets=[0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0, 2.5, 5.0, 10.0, 30.0, 60.0, 120.0], )





Time-to-first-token (TTFT) — time before first token is generated


Critical for streaming UX — users perceive this as "thinking time"


Should be <500ms for good UX


TTFT_HISTOGRAM = Histogram( "llm_ttft_seconds", "Time to first token in seconds", buckets=[0.05, 0.1, 0.2, 0.5, 1.0, 2.0, 5.0, 10.0], )





Number of tokens generated per request

GENERATION_LENGTH = Histogram( "llm_generation_tokens", "Number of tokens generated per request", buckets=[10, 50, 100, 250, 500, 1000, 2000, 4000, 8000], )

PROMPT_LENGTH = Histogram( "llm_prompt_tokens", "Number of prompt tokens per request", buckets=[50, 100, 250, 500, 1000, 2000, 5000, 10000, 50000], )

Used for: active requests, memory usage, GPU utilization


Number of requests currently being processed


Use: detect traffic surges, check concurrency

GPU utilization percentage (0-100%)


Use: detect bottlenecks, identify idle GPU


GPU_UTILIZATION = Gauge( "llm_gpu_utilization_percent", "GPU compute utilization percent", labelnames=["gpu_id"], )

KV_CACHE_UTILIZATION = Gauge( "llm_kv_cache_utilization", "KV cache utilization percent", )

THROUGHPUT = Gauge( "llm_throughput_tokens_per_second", "Generation throughput in tokens per second", )





SUMMARY — similar to Histogram but also tracks quantiles


Use for: SLI monitoring (service level indicators)


Request latency with pre-computed quantiles


This is what you'd use for SLO monitoring (p50, p95, p99)


LATENCY_SUMMARY = Summary( "llm_latency_summary_seconds", "Request latency summary with quantiles", # Automatically computed quantiles: # 0.5 (median), 0.95, 0.99 # Summaries compute these on the client side (lower overhead than histograms) )





=============================================================================


METRIC RECORDING FUNCTIONS


=============================================================================


def record_request_metrics( latency: float, ttft: float, prompt_tokens: int, generated_tokens: int, success: bool = True, error_type: str = None, ): """Record all metrics for a single inference request.

Args (key/value explanations): latency: Total time from request receipt to completion (seconds) Target: <2s for chat, <30s for long generation ttft: Time to first token (seconds) Target: <500ms for good UX prompt_tokens: Number of tokens in the input prompt Affects TTFT (longer prompts = higher TTFT) generated_tokens: Number of tokens in the output Affects total latency (more tokens = longer) success: Whether the request completed without error error_type: Type of error if not successful """ # Increment counters TOTAL_REQUESTS.inc() TOTAL_TOKENS_GENERATED.inc(generated_tokens) if not success: TOTAL_ERRORS.labels(error_type=error_type or "unknown").inc() # Observe histograms LATENCY_HISTOGRAM.observe(latency) TTFT_HISTOGRAM.observe(ttft) GENERATION_LENGTH.observe(generated_tokens) PROMPT_LENGTH.observe(prompt_tokens) # Observe summary LATENCY_SUMMARY.observe(latency)

def collect_system_metrics(): """Collect GPU and system metrics every N seconds.

Run this in a background thread at 15-30 second intervals. These metrics are point-in-time (Gauges), not cumulative. """ # GPU metrics (using PyTorch) if torch.cuda.is_available(): for gpu_id in range(torch.cuda.device_count()): # Memory used in GB memory_used = torch.cuda.memory_allocated(gpu_id) / 1e9 GPU_MEMORY_USED.labels(gpu_id=str(gpu_id)).set(memory_used) # GPU utilization (nvidia-smi or PyTorch) try: # Requires pynvml: pip install nvidia-ml-py from pynvml import nvmlInit, nvmlDeviceGetHandleByIndex, nvmlDeviceGetUtilizationRates nvmlInit() handle = nvmlDeviceGetHandleByIndex(gpu_id) util = nvmlDeviceGetUtilizationRates(handle) GPU_UTILIZATION.labels(gpu_id=str(gpu_id)).set(util.gpu) except: pass # nvml not available # CPU and system memory cpu_mem = psutil.virtual_memory() CPU_MEMORY_USED.set(cpu_mem.used / 1e9)





=============================================================================


ALERT RULES — Thresholds with explanations


=============================================================================


ALERT_RULES = """





Alert Rules (Prometheus format)


High error rate — indicates infrastructure or model issues


Rule: >5% error rate over 5 minutes


Action: check GPU health, model loading, API gateway


alert: HighErrorRate expr: rate(llm_errors_total[5m]) / rate(llm_requests_total[5m]) > 0.05 for: 2m annotations: summary: "Error rate above 5%"





High latency — indicates overload or hardware issue


Rule: p99 latency > 10s over 5 minutes


Action: scale up replicas, check GPU utilization, optimize generation params


alert: HighLatencyP99 expr: histogram_quantile(0.99, rate(llm_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) > 10 for: 2m annotations: summary: "P99 latency above 10s"





Low throughput — indicates bottleneck


Rule: throughput < 10 tokens/sec over 5 minutes


Action: check GPU utilization, increase batch size, check for CPU bottleneck


alert: LowThroughput expr: rate(llm_tokens_generated_total[5m]) < 10 for: 5m annotations: summary: "Throughput below 10 tokens/sec"





OOM errors — indicates memory leak or under-provisioned GPU


Rule: any OOM error in last 5 minutes


Action: reduce gpu_memory_utilization, check for memory leak, increase GPU count


alert: OutOfMemory expr: rate(llm_errors_total{error_type="oom"}[5m]) > 0 for: 1m annotations: summary: "Out of memory errors detected"





Queue growing — indicates insufficient replicas


Rule: queue depth > 100 for over 5 minutes


Action: scale up the number of replicas


alert: QueueGrowing expr: llm_queue_depth > 100 for: 5m annotations: summary: "Request queue depth above 100"





GPU memory leak — memory increasing over time


Rule: GPU memory increasing >5% over 30 minutes without corresponding load


Action: restart server, check for memory leak in model or attention


alert: GPU_MemoryLeakDetected expr: deriv(llm_gpu_memory_used_gb[30m]) > 0.05 for: 10m annotations: summary: "GPU memory gradually increasing — possible leak" """

45.1 Logging & Structured Observability


Beyond Prometheus metrics, robust observability requires structured logging, log aggregation across distributed workers, and request correlation IDs for tracing.





45.1.1 Structured JSON Logging with python-json-logger


```python





pip install python-json-logger


from pythonjsonlogger import jsonlogger import logging import sys from datetime import datetime, timezone





=============================================================================


Structured JSON Logger for ML Pipelines


=============================================================================


def setup_json_logger( name: str = "ml_pipeline", level: int = logging.INFO, output_file: str = None, add_console: bool = True, ) -> logging.Logger: """ Configure a logger that outputs JSON lines for machine consumption.

This format is directly ingestible by: - ELK Stack (Elasticsearch, Logstash, Kibana) - Grafana Loki - Google Cloud Logging - Datadog / Splunk Each log line is a JSON object: { "timestamp": "2026-05-22T10:30:00.123Z", "level": "INFO", "logger": "ml_pipeline", "message": "Training step completed", "module": "train", "function": "train_step", "step": 1000, "loss": 2.34, "learning_rate": 3e-5 } """ logger = logging.getLogger(name) logger.setLevel(level) logger.handlers.clear() # JSON formatter with custom fields formatter = jsonlogger.JsonFormatter( fmt=( "%(timestamp)s %(level)s %(name)s %(message)s " "%(module)s %(funcName)s %(lineno)d" ), timestamp=True, # Include ISO 8601 timestamp datefmt="iso", # ISO format: 2026-05-22T10:30:00.123Z # Reserved attrs control which standard fields appear: reserved_attrs=("message", "name", "level", "module", "funcName", "lineno"), ) # Console handler (human + machine readable) if add_console: handler = logging.StreamHandler(sys.stdout) handler.setFormatter(formatter) logger.addHandler(handler) # File handler (JSON Lines — one JSON object per line) if output_file: file_handler = logging.FileHandler(output_file, mode="a") file_handler.setFormatter(formatter) logger.addHandler(file_handler) # Wrap standard logging methods to accept extra kwargs # Now you can call: logger.info("step done", extra={"loss": 2.3, "step": 100}) return logger





Usage in training pipeline:


log = setup_json_logger( name="wfb_training", level=logging.DEBUG, # DEBUG for full trace, INFO for production output_file="logs/training.jsonl", add_console=True, )





Standard logging with structured extras


log.info("Training started", extra={ "num_params": 7e9, "batch_size": 4, "max_steps": 100000, })

log.info("Step completed", extra={ "step": 1000, "loss": 2.345, "perplexity": 10.43, "learning_rate": 3e-5, "grad_norm": 0.87, "throughput_tok_s": 12500, "gpu_mem_gb": 42.5, })

log.warning("Gradient spike detected", extra={ "step": 2500, "grad_norm": 15.2, "threshold": 10.0, })

try: risky_operation() except Exception as e: log.error("Training failed", extra={ "step": global_step, "exception_type": type(e).name, "exception_msg": str(e), "traceback": traceback.format_exc(), }) raise ```





45.1.2 Log Levels & Distributed Log Aggregation


In multi-GPU/multi-node training, logs from all workers must be aggregated. The key patterns are:

```python import logging import socket from typing import Optional





=============================================================================


Distributed-aware Logger — controls log level per rank


=============================================================================


class DistributedLogger: """ Logger that adjusts verbosity based on the distributed rank.

Rules: - Rank 0: full logging (INFO + above) - Rank > 0: only WARNING + above (reduces noise in distributed logs) - Critical errors: all ranks log (for crash debugging) Usage: logger = DistributedLogger() logger.info("Only rank 0 sees this") # Suppressed on workers logger.warning("All ranks see warnings") # Logged everywhere logger.critical("All ranks see critical") # Always logged """ def __init__( self, name: str = "distributed_training", rank: Optional[int] = None, world_size: Optional[int] = None, log_dir: str = "logs", json_format: bool = True, ): # Detect rank & world size from environment (works with torchrun) self.rank = rank if rank is not None else int( os.environ.get("RANK", os.environ.get("LOCAL_RANK", 0)) ) self.world_size = world_size if world_size is not None else int( os.environ.get("WORLD_SIZE", 1) ) self.hostname = socket.gethostname() # Create a per-rank JSON logger self.logger = setup_json_logger( name=f"{name}_rank{self.rank}", level=logging.INFO if self.rank == 0 else logging.WARNING, output_file=f"{log_dir}/train_rank{self.rank}.jsonl", add_console=(self.rank == 0), # Only rank 0 logs to console ) def debug(self, msg: str, **kwargs): """DEBUG level — only rank 0, only in non-production.""" if self.rank == 0: self.logger.debug(msg, extra=kwargs) def info(self, msg: str, **kwargs): """INFO level — rank 0 only (reduces log volume by world_size-1).""" if self.rank == 0: self.logger.info(msg, extra={**kwargs, "rank": self.rank}) def warning(self, msg: str, **kwargs): """WARNING — all ranks log warnings (suspicious events on any worker).""" self.logger.warning(msg, extra={**kwargs, "rank": self.rank, "host": self.hostname}) def error(self, msg: str, **kwargs): """ERROR — all ranks log errors (critical for debugging failures).""" self.logger.error(msg, extra={**kwargs, "rank": self.rank, "host": self.hostname}) def critical(self, msg: str, **kwargs): """CRITICAL — all ranks, highest urgency.""" self.logger.critical(msg, extra={**kwargs, "rank": self.rank, "host": self.hostname}) def metric(self, name: str, value: float, step: int, tags: dict = None): """ Log a structured metric that can be parsed by monitoring tools. These are emitted as INFO level on rank 0 only. """ if self.rank == 0: self.logger.info(f"metric:{name}", extra={ "metric_name": name, "metric_value": value, "step": step, **(tags or {}), })





=============================================================================


Log Aggregation — merge per-rank logs into a single view


=============================================================================


def aggregate_logs(log_dir: str, output_path: str = "logs/aggregated.jsonl"): """ Merge per-rank JSONL logs, sorting by timestamp.

After this, you can do: import pandas as pd df = pd.read_json("logs/aggregated.jsonl", lines=True) """ import glob import json log_files = sorted(glob.glob(f"{log_dir}/train_rank*.jsonl")) all_entries = [] for fpath in log_files: with open(fpath) as f: for line in f: try: entry = json.loads(line.strip()) all_entries.append(entry) except json.JSONDecodeError: continue # Sort by timestamp all_entries.sort(key=lambda e: e.get("timestamp", "")) # Write merged output with open(output_path, "w") as f: for entry in all_entries: f.write(json.dumps(entry, default=str) + "\n") print(f"Aggregated {len(all_entries)} log entries from {len(log_files)} ranks " f"→ {output_path}") return all_entries





=============================================================================


Distributed Log Aggregation with a Log Server (single-node pattern)


=============================================================================


class LogAggregationServer: """ Simple log aggregation server that collects logs from all ranks over a TCP socket and writes them to a single file.

Alternative: use a proper log shipper (Fluentd, Vector, Logstash). """ def __init__(self, port: int = 9999, output_path: str = "logs/aggregated.jsonl"): self.port = port self.output_path = output_path self.entries = [] def start(self): import socket import threading server = socket.socket(socket.AF_INET, socket.SOCK_STREAM) server.bind(("0.0.0.0", self.port)) server.listen(8) # Max 8 workers def handle_client(conn): with conn: while True: data = conn.recv(4096) if not data: break self.entries.append(data.decode()) # Write to file immediately with open(self.output_path, "a") as f: f.write(data.decode() + "\n") threads = [] for _ in range(8): t = threading.Thread(target=handle_client, args=(server.accept(),)) t.start() threads.append(t)





=============================================================================


Log Level Decision Matrix


=============================================================================


LOG_LEVEL_GUIDE = """ Log Level Usage Guide for ML Pipelines:

DEBUG: - Per-batch metrics (loss, grad norm for every step) - Tensor shapes and dtypes during data loading - Device placement decisions (offloading, checkpointing) - NOT enabled in production (high volume)

INFO: - Training start/stop/resume - Checkpoint saves and loads - Epoch/step completion (every N steps, not per-step) - Learning rate changes - Dataset loaded, model compiled - Validation results

WARNING: - Gradient spikes (norm > threshold) - Learning rate reset due to loss divergence - Slow data loading (num_workers underperforming) - NCCL communication warnings - Checkpoint save failure (retry)

ERROR: - GPU out-of-memory (OOM) - Data corruption detected - NCCL timeout or connection loss - Model NaN/Inf in loss or gradients - Failed checkpoint load - DataLoader worker crash

CRITICAL: - Loss diverges to NaN/Inf (training must stop) - Multi-node connection lost - Disk full (cannot save checkpoint) - Power/temperature shutdown imminent - Ranks out of sync (deadlock detected) """ ```





45.1.3 Correlation IDs for Request Tracing


Correlation IDs (trace IDs) let you trace a single request through the entire pipeline: API gateway → inference server → model forward → response streaming.

```python import uuid import contextvars import logging from typing import Optional





=============================================================================


Correlation ID Context — propagates trace ID through async/sync code


=============================================================================


Context variable (thread-safe and asyncio-safe)


_correlation_id: contextvars.ContextVar[str] = contextvars.ContextVar( "correlation_id", default=None )

def get_correlation_id() -> Optional[str]: """Get the current request's correlation ID.""" return _correlation_id.get()

def set_correlation_id(cid: Optional[str] = None) -> str: """Set the correlation ID for the current context (request).""" if cid is None: cid = str(uuid.uuid4()) _correlation_id.set(cid) return cid





=============================================================================


Logging Filter — automatically injects correlation ID into log records


=============================================================================


class CorrelationIDFilter(logging.Filter): """ Logging filter that appends the correlation ID to every log record.

Usage: logger.addFilter(CorrelationIDFilter()) # Now every log line automatically has "correlation_id" field """ def filter(self, record: logging.LogRecord) -> bool: cid = get_correlation_id() record.correlation_id = cid or "none" return True





=============================================================================


Decorator for automatic correlation ID on API endpoints


=============================================================================


def with_correlation_id(func): """ Decorator for request handlers. Creates a new correlation ID for each request and ensures it's set before the handler runs.

Works with FastAPI, Flask, or plain functions. """ from functools import wraps @wraps(func) def wrapper(*args, **kwargs): cid = set_correlation_id() try: return func(*args, **kwargs) finally: # Clean up after request completes _correlation_id.set(None) return wrapper





=============================================================================


Stream handler that wraps a generator with correlation ID


=============================================================================


def with_trace_id(stream_generator): """ Wrap an SSE/streaming generator to include trace IDs in each chunk.

Useful for debugging streaming inference responses: - Correlate log entries with the streaming response - Track which GPU processed which request """ cid = get_correlation_id() or set_correlation_id() for chunk in stream_generator: # Inject trace ID into response metadata yield { "correlation_id": cid, "data": chunk, "timestamp": datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat(), }





=============================================================================


Integration Example: FastAPI + Correlation ID + Structured Logging


=============================================================================


""" from fastapi import FastAPI, Request from fastapi.responses import StreamingResponse

app = FastAPI() log = setup_json_logger("api_server") log.addFilter(CorrelationIDFilter())

@app.post("/v1/chat/completions") @with_correlation_id async def chat_completion(request: Request): cid = get_correlation_id() body = await request.json()

log.info("Inference request received", extra={ "correlation_id": cid, "model": body.get("model"), "prompt_length": len(body.get("messages", [])), "max_tokens": body.get("max_tokens", 1024), "ip": request.client.host, }) async def generate(): # The correlation ID is automatically included in all log calls # within this generator via the context variable async for token in model.generate(body["messages"]): log.debug("Token generated", extra={ "correlation_id": cid, "token_id": token.id, }) yield token return StreamingResponse( with_trace_id(generate()), media_type="text/event-stream", )

"""





=============================================================================


Log-based Trace Visualization


=============================================================================


def extract_trace(correlation_id: str, log_file: str = "logs/training.jsonl"): """ Extract all log entries for a specific correlation ID.

This gives you a complete trace of a single request's lifecycle: Example output: 2026-05-22T10:30:00.123Z INFO Request received (model=gpt-4, prompt_len=128) 2026-05-22T10:30:00.200Z INFO KV cache allocated (tokens=128, gpu=0) 2026-05-22T10:30:00.250Z INFO Prefill complete (tokens=128, time=50ms) 2026-05-22T10:30:00.350Z INFO Token 1 generated (time=100ms) 2026-05-22T10:30:00.400Z INFO Token 2 generated (time=50ms) ... 2026-05-22T10:30:05.000Z INFO Request complete (total_tokens=256, time=4.88s) """ import json trace = [] with open(log_file) as f: for line in f: entry = json.loads(line) if entry.get("correlation_id") == correlation_id: trace.append(entry) trace.sort(key=lambda e: e.get("timestamp", "")) print(f"Trace for correlation_id={correlation_id}:") print("-" * 80) for entry in trace: ts = entry.get("timestamp", "?") level = entry.get("level", "?") msg = entry.get("message", "?") extra = {k: v for k, v in entry.items() if k not in ("timestamp", "level", "message", "logger", "module", "funcName", "lineno", "correlation_id")} extra_str = " ".join(f"{k}={v}" for k, v in extra.items()) print(f"{ts} [{level:8s}] {msg} {extra_str}") return trace

```





45.1.4 Custom Logging Handlers for ML Pipelines


```python





=============================================================================


Metric Logging Handler — emit structured metrics to external systems


=============================================================================


class MetricsLoggingHandler(logging.Handler): """ Custom logging handler that extracts numeric metrics from log records and forwards them to a metrics backend (Prometheus, Datadog, StatsD).

Pattern: logging.info("metric:loss=2.34", extra={"step": 1000}) → handler parses "metric:" prefix and sends to Prometheus Gauge """ def __init__(self, metrics_prefix: str = "ml"): super().__init__(level=logging.INFO) self.metrics_prefix = metrics_prefix self._gauges = {} # Cache Prometheus Gauges def emit(self, record: logging.LogRecord): message = record.getMessage() # Only process metric-prefixed messages if not message.startswith("metric:"): return # Parse "metric:name=value" try: _, metric_str = message.split(":", 1) name, value_str = metric_str.split("=", 1) value = float(value_str) step = getattr(record, "step", 0) except (ValueError, TypeError): return # Invalid metric format # Emit to Prometheus (if available) self._emit_prometheus(name, value, record) # Emit to console (structured JSON) self._emit_structured(name, value, step, record) def _emit_prometheus(self, name: str, value: float, record: logging.LogRecord): try: from prometheus_client import Gauge # Create or retrieve cached Gauge gauge_name = f"{self.metrics_prefix}_{name}" if gauge_name not in self._gauges: self._gauges[gauge_name] = Gauge( gauge_name, f"ML metric: {name}", labelnames=["step"], ) self._gauges[gauge_name].labels(step=str(getattr(record, "step", 0))).set(value) except ImportError: pass # Prometheus not installed def _emit_structured(self, name: str, value: float, step: int, record: logging.LogRecord): """Also log as structured JSON for file-based analysis.""" import json entry = { "timestamp": self.format(record), "type": "metric", "metric_name": name, "metric_value": value, "step": step, "tags": { k: v for k, v in record.__dict__.items() if k not in ("args", "created", "exc_info", "exc_text", "filename", "funcName", "levelname", "levelno", "lineno", "module", "msecs", "message", "msg", "name", "pathname", "process", "processName", "relativeCreated", "stack_info", "thread", "threadName", "step") }, } print(json.dumps(entry, default=str)) # In production, write to a file





=============================================================================


Training Progress Handler — TQDM integration


=============================================================================


class TQDMProgressHandler(logging.Handler): """ Logging handler that updates a tqdm progress bar with training metrics.

This keeps your console clean: progress bar shows live metrics, while JSON logs go to file for analysis. Usage: progress_handler = TQDMProgressHandler(total_steps=100000) logger.addHandler(progress_handler) for step in train_loop: logger.info("step", extra={"loss": loss, "lr": lr}) # → tqdm bar updates automatically """ def __init__(self, total_steps: int, desc: str = "Training"): super().__init__(level=logging.INFO) from tqdm import tqdm self.progress = tqdm( total=total_steps, desc=desc, unit="step", bar_format="{l_bar}{bar}| {n_fmt}/{total_fmt} [{elapsed}<{remaining}, {rate_fmt}] " "{postfix}", ) self.current_step = 0 def emit(self, record: logging.LogRecord): step = getattr(record, "step", None) if step is not None: # Update progress to current step update_by = step - self.current_step if update_by > 0: self.progress.update(update_by) self.current_step = step # Update postfix with metrics metrics = {} for attr in ("loss", "lr", "grad_norm", "throughput", "perplexity"): val = getattr(record, attr, None) if val is not None: metrics[attr] = val if metrics: self.progress.set_postfix(**metrics)





=============================================================================


Slack/Webhook Alert Handler — send critical alerts to Slack/PagerDuty


=============================================================================


class AlertWebhookHandler(logging.Handler): """ Sends CRITICAL and ERROR log records to a webhook (Slack, Discord, PagerDuty).

Filters to only high-severity events to avoid alert fatigue. Rate-limited to prevent webhook spam. """ def __init__(self, webhook_url: str, min_level=logging.ERROR, cooldown_sec: int = 60): super().__init__(level=min_level) self.webhook_url = webhook_url self.cooldown_sec = cooldown_sec self.last_alert_time = 0 def emit(self, record: logging.LogRecord): import time now = time.time() # Rate limit: don't send more than one alert per cooldown period if now - self.last_alert_time < self.cooldown_sec: return self.last_alert_time = now # Format the alert payload message = self.format(record) payload = { "text": f"[{record.levelname}] ML Pipeline Alert\n" f"Message: {record.getMessage()}\n" f"Logger: {record.name}\n" f"Module: {record.module}:{record.lineno}\n" f"Extra: { {k: v for k, v in record.__dict__.items() if k not in logging.LogRecord( None, None, "", 0, None, None, None ).__dict__} }", } try: import requests requests.post(self.webhook_url, json=payload, timeout=5) except Exception: pass # Don't crash the main process if webhook fails





=============================================================================


Complete Logging Pipeline Example


=============================================================================


def configure_ml_logging_pipeline( experiment_name: str, log_dir: str = "logs", slack_webhook: str = None, total_steps: int = 100000, ): """ Configure a complete logging pipeline for ML training with: - Structured JSON logging to file (machine parsable) - Console output with tqdm progress (human readable) - Metrics → Prometheus (for dashboards) - Alerts → Slack/PagerDuty (for critical failures) - Correlation IDs (for request tracing) """ import logging

# Root ML logger logger = logging.getLogger(f"ml.{experiment_name}") logger.setLevel(logging.DEBUG) logger.handlers.clear() # 1. JSON file handler (all levels, machine-readable) json_handler = logging.FileHandler(f"{log_dir}/{experiment_name}.jsonl", mode="a") json_handler.setLevel(logging.DEBUG) json_handler.setFormatter(jsonlogger.JsonFormatter( fmt="%(timestamp)s %(level)s %(name)s %(message)s", timestamp=True, )) logger.addHandler(json_handler) # 2. Console handler (INFO+, human-readable) console = logging.StreamHandler(sys.stdout) console.setLevel(logging.INFO) console.setFormatter(logging.Formatter( "%(asctime)s [%(levelname)s] %(message)s", datefmt="%H:%M:%S", )) logger.addHandler(console) # 3. TQDM progress bar (for interactive sessions) if total_steps > 0: tqdm_handler = TQDMProgressHandler(total_steps=total_steps, desc=experiment_name) tqdm_handler.setLevel(logging.INFO) logger.addHandler(tqdm_handler) # 4. Metrics handler (Prometheus forwarding) metrics_handler = MetricsLoggingHandler(metrics_prefix=experiment_name) metrics_handler.setLevel(logging.INFO) logger.addHandler(metrics_handler) # 5. Alert webhook handler (ERROR+, rate-limited) if slack_webhook: alert_handler = AlertWebhookHandler( webhook_url=slack_webhook, min_level=logging.ERROR, cooldown_sec=60, ) alert_handler.setLevel(logging.ERROR) logger.addHandler(alert_handler) # 6. Correlation ID filter (attaches to every log record) logger.addFilter(CorrelationIDFilter()) return logger

Observability Stack Summary


=============================================================================


OBSERVABILITY_SUMMARY = """ Layer Tool Purpose Cost ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Logging python-json-logger Structured JSON logs to file Free Metrics Prometheus Real-time numeric metrics Free Dashboards Grafana Visualize metrics + logs Free Alerting AlertManager Route alerts (Slack, PagerDuty) Free Tracing Correlation IDs Request-level trace across pipeline Free Log agg. Vector/Fluentd Ship logs from all nodes → central Free Model registry MLflow / WandB Version models + experiments Free/Paid Cost tracking Custom Track GPU-hours, token spend Custom """ ```
